title: Senior Google Ads Specialist | International Ecommerce | Berlin ASAP
description:
ennovationHUB is a growing international e-commerce group in the home & living sector, with furniture at the heart of our business. From our hubs in Belgrade, Barcelona, and London, we reach customers across the UK, North America, the EU, and APAC. 

With a target of €160m+ in annual revenue by 2027, we are looking for a Senior Google Ads Specialist to join us as soon as possible and lead Google Ads performance for one of our portfolio brands. You will have direct accountability for growing revenue, improving advertising efficiency, and delivering profitable results. 

About the opportunity 

You will join a multi-brand international e-commerce business with significant advertising budgets and campaigns spanning multiple markets. This gives you the opportunity to work at scale and see how your decisions influence revenue and profitability. 

Google Ads is already an important contributor to our growth. We are looking for someone who enjoys the complexity of international e-commerce, is confident working with large datasets, and can identify opportunities that lead to measurable improvements. 

Through analysis, testing, and hands-on optimisation, you will help strengthen an established channel and support its continued growth. You will work closely with our Head of Performance Marketing, creative team, and data specialists to ensure campaigns deliver results today and scale efficiently over time. 

What you will be responsible for: 

- Take full ownership of Google Ads results for one e-commerce brand across international markets 

- Manage and optimise campaigns across Search, Shopping, Performance Max, and other relevant campaign types 

- Track and improve key metrics, including ROAS, CPA, conversion rate, revenue, and profitability 

- Deliver growth and efficiency improvements within your assigned portfolio 

- Identify opportunities across product ranges, categories, markets, and audience segments 

- Translate campaign analysis into practical recommendations and actions 

- Audit accounts and implement ongoing performance improvements 

- Collaborate with developers and analytics teams to ensure dependable tracking and measurement 

- Partner with creative and content teams to improve ad effectiveness and landing page performance 

- Support budget allocation, forecasting, and performance reporting 

- Keep up with platform changes, AI-driven advertising features, and industry best practices 

- Contribute to structured testing and experimentation that improves long-term account performance 

The impact you can make: 

Our Google Ads activity already delivers results. Your role will be to build on that success by finding new opportunities, improving efficiency, and expanding what works.

We operate in a competitive e-commerce market where incremental gains can have a meaningful effect on business performance. You will be expected to connect campaign decisions with commercial outcomes and take responsibility for the results.

You will work with experienced colleagues who act quickly and care about execution. We encourage independent thinking, decisions grounded in data, and constructive challenges to existing assumptions. You will be trusted to make decisions and contribute directly to the growth of the business. 

This role is open only to candidates with in-house e-commerce experience. Applicants whose primary Google Ads experience comes from agencies, consultancies, or freelance work will not be considered.

We are seeking someone who has been directly responsible for performance within an e-commerce company, with success measured through revenue, profitability, customer acquisition, and long-term growth.

You should understand the commercial context behind campaign performance and be comfortable owning both the decisions and the execution needed to deliver results. 

What you will bring: 

- At least 2 years of hands-on Google Ads campaign management experience 

- Proven experience managing Google Ads for an e-commerce business, with direct responsibility for performance and profitability 

- Strong experience across Search, Shopping, and Performance Max 

- A background working within an in-house e-commerce team 

- Confidence analysing large datasets and identifying actionable opportunities 

- A strong understanding of attribution, tracking, and performance measurement 

- Familiarity with Google Analytics 4, Google Tag Manager, and Google Merchant Center 

- Strong analytical ability and careful attention to detail 

- Fluent written and spoken English 

- The ability to manage changing priorities in a fast-moving environment 

- Curiosity, initiative, and a continuous improvement mindset 

- Confidence working independently, making decisions, and taking ownership 

- A willingness to adopt AI and automation as we expand their use throughout the business 

- Availability to join immediately or as soon as possible 

Your working style: 

You combine senior-level thinking with practical execution and remain closely involved in campaign performance. You use data to reach clear decisions and turn insights into action.

You are curious about what drives results and consistently look for ways to improve them. You can balance longer-term strategy with daily optimisation, keeping your focus on outcomes and business growth.

You enjoy building and scaling campaigns, taking responsibility for performance, and helping an established channel reach its next stage of growth.

International collaboration and travel: 

Our wider team operates across London, Belgrade, Barcelona, Frankfurt, Oxfordshire, Istanbul, and Guangzhou. We are continuing to invest in our team presence as the business expands.

You will be expected to travel approximately every 4-8 weeks to Belgrade, Barcelona, London, or other team locations. These visits bring colleagues together for planning sessions, workshops, team gatherings, and strategic discussions.

Although most work is carried out remotely, we value spending time together in person to collaborate and plan as the company scales. 

This is a long-term opportunity to play a meaningful part in growing an international e-commerce business over the coming years. 

Our culture at ennovationHUB: 

We value: 

- Taking responsibility and following through 

- Putting plans into action 

- Clear and direct communication 

- Learning through practical experience 

We welcome people from diverse backgrounds who take pride in their work, own their contribution, and help the business move forward.

- Du skalierst profitabel und findest Wege, mehr Spend bei gleichem NC-ROAS auszugeben.

- Du fährst Sales-Events wie die Black Week mit sechsstelligem Budget selbst.

- Du analysierst die Performance in Triple Whale, Meta, Google und Shopify und gibst deine Learnings direkt an unsere Creative Strategists weiter.

- Du entwickelst unsere Automationen mit KI-Routinen weiter und testest neue Kanäle.

- Mindestens 3 Jahre Media Buying bei einer E-Commerce-Brand oder Performance-Agentur.

- Du denkst in Zahlen (Triple Whale oder vergleichbar, MER, Post-Purchase-Survey) und nutzt KI selbstverständlich für Analysen und Automationen.

- Der Account wird jeden Tag geprüft, auch samstags und sonntags. Deine Stunden verteilst du dafür frei über die Woche.

- Du sprichst fließend Deutsch und gutes Englisch.

title: Chief of Staff, Data Science & Analytics
description:
Brief info about Vinted 

Our mission is to make second-hand the first choice, and we're looking for people who want to help us get there. Every day, we work together to help our members buy and sell pre-loved clothing and lifestyle items, giving each piece a second life – or even a third. 
The Vinted Group is made up of three business units that support this mission:

Vinted Marketplace is Europe’s leading platform for second-hand fashion and a go-to destination for all kinds of pre-loved items, with a growing range of categories. Our platform connects millions of members across 20+ markets, helping great items find a new life.

Vinted Go enhances the shipping experience with a vast network of over 500,000 pick-up and drop-off points, partnering with more than 60 carriers across Europe, with added services like item verification for peace of mind on high-value pieces.

Vinted Pay is the newest part of the Vinted Group, dedicated to bringing secure, reliable payments to buyers and sellers across Europe. Seamlessly integrated into the Vinted app, it helps keep every transaction safe, efficient, and easy for our members.

Founded in 2008 in Lithuania, Vinted began as a way for friends to find new homes for clothes they no longer needed. In 2019, we became Lithuania's first unicorn! Today, our headquarters remain in Vilnius, and we've grown with offices across Europe, supported by a team of over 2,000 people. 

Information about the position 

The Chief of Staff is part of the senior leadership team of the Vinted-wide Data Science & Analytics function. Your primary role will be to build an aligned, engaged, and impactful team while ensuring the successful management and execution of key data strategies and initiatives. The Chief of Staff reports directly to the Vice President of Data Science & Analytics (“VP of DSA”) and acts as a trusted advisor and partner in ensuring that the department runs smoothly, efficiently, and effectively.

This is a fixed-term (maternity cover) position for approximately 1 year. 

In this position, you’ll 

- Serve as a trusted advisor to the VP of DSA, providing advice and guidance on all matters within the function (e.g. operating cadence, planning, problem analysis, communication). 

- Own and run the function’s reporting cycles end-to-end (e.g. QBRs, OKR meetings, DSA All Hands); including content creation, preparation, facilitation, and follow-ups.

- Be responsible for coordinating the development and driving the execution of key function strategies and initiatives (e.g. data related initiatives that drive long-term impact), and supporting broader cross-functional and organisational initiatives that involve DSA (e.g. reorganisations and operating model shifts).

- Oversee and manage recurrent DSA operations (e.g. DSA’s onboarding programme as well as the Data Science & Analytics Academy programme).

- Own the delivery of key functional events, including planning groups and agenda development (e.g. offsites, function week).

- Be accountable for maintaining an efficient operating model by ensuring processes, policies, and ceremonies are in place and effective, fostering an aligned, engaged, and impactful team.

- Support the DSA leadership team on the integration of AI into our data team’s (300+ team members) workflows.

- Be the driving force behind the senior and extended DSA leadership teams; coordinating and managing meetings, keeping track of decisions and pending relevant actions, holding the group accountable, and ensuring follow-through.

- (Co-) author key documents on function-related topics, ranging from vision and strategy papers to process and standards documentation, based on high-level instructions and discussions with the team and stakeholders.

- Conduct research and analysis on industry trends, best practices, and emerging technologies related to the function, and provide recommendations to the DSA leadership team.

- Own the organisation and documentation of the function’s governance (e.g., Google Groups, Drive, Confluence spaces, Slack Channels).

About you 

- Significant experience in strategy, consulting, or strategic transformation roles, with a track record of success in project management, management engagement, and strategic planning.

- Strong analytical skills, with the ability to break complex initiatives and challenges into manageable deliverables.

- Strong organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects and initiatives simultaneously.

- Proven leadership and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work collaboratively and build relationships across all levels of the organisation.

- Strong facilitation and moderation skills, with experience designing and leading workshops to discuss strategic priorities, build alignment, and drive decision-making.

- Comfortable interpreting aggregate (analytical) data and turning it into actional conclusions – but advanced data analysis skills are not required.

- Excellent communication skills, with the ability to effectively convey complex information to both technical and non-technical audiences.

- Hands on and detail-oriented problem solver, able to identify operational gaps and inefficiencies.

- Adaptable and comfortable operating under ambiguity, with the ability to pivot quickly, reprioritise effectively, and respond to emerging challenges with a solutions-oriented mindset.

Work perks

- 30 days of paid annual leave

- Newest MacBook models

- Confidential Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for you and your family

- Home office support: we provide IT workstation equipment and a personal budget of up to €540 for home workplace furniture

- Lunch benefit per your workday

- Pension Plan with Vinted matching 150% of your chosen contribution

- Supplemental Private Health Insurance

Working at Vinted 

Workation policy 

Better balance holidays with workdays by working remotely! Up to 90 days per year in the EU, of these, 21 days can be spent globally. For non-EU citizens, it's 21 days worldwide. This can be combined with time off for vacation or personal time.

Individual learning budget 

Each year, you’ll be given a learning budget (starting at €3,000), and a total of up to 10 working days over a 2-year period to support your personal and professional development.

Hybrid work 

Our hybrid model, with 2 recommended office days a week, gives you and your team the flexibility to decide if and when you want to work from home, and when to catch up in person.

Equal opportunity

title: Senior Associate - Venture & Growth (m/f/d)
description:
Senior Associate - Venture & Growth (m/f/d)

Join the team rewriting the rules in private markets. 

Moonfare delivers what few others can: the highly sought-after funds and hidden-gem investments that go beyond what most private banks offer. Every opportunity is subjected to a ruthless vetting process; the bar is unforgivingly high. The result? Institutional-quality portfolios for investors who demand more.

Our team combines finance veterans with talent from tech, consulting, law and industries you’d never expect. Headquartered in Berlin, we operate from eight offices across Europe, the US and Asia.

If you're ready to build what's next in private markets, let's talk.

Mission: 

Turn Moonfare's access to the world's leading venture managers into a steady, well-underwritten flow of single-company investments our clients can actually buy.

About the role: 

A significant share of Moonfare's AuM sits in venture and growth, and the direct side of it, co-investments and secondaries in VC-backed companies, is where the business is growing fastest. Right now that dealflow arrives faster than we can review it, which puts the deployment of our proprietary funds at risk and caps how far the direct platform can scale. The scope of this role begins the moment an opportunity reaches us and ends when the deal closes, so operations sits outside it, as does the client raise itself. Your first year is weighted towards screening, pipeline and diligence, with the sourcing and business development side building from there as your market view and relationships deepen. You will work alongside senior members of the team rather than alone, and what moves forward is decided together.

The team: 

Venture & Growth sits inside Moonfare's Investment team and runs two connected things. One is a multi-manager vehicle making primary fund investments into leading VC and growth managers across the US and Europe, where we have historically backed Founders Fund, a16z, Accel, Lightspeed, Khosla and General Catalyst. The other is the direct programme of co-investments and secondaries that those manager relationships generate, which is where this role's centre of gravity sits. You will report to the Head of VC & Direct Investing and work daily with the commercial team, who depend on you for qualified dealflow, and alongside Legal and Operations to close deals and launch the SPVs we distribute on the platform.

You will: 

- Own the direct deal pipeline. Everything from the moment an opportunity reaches us through to close is yours to run, so nothing sits unscreened and no access window quietly closes while we are still deciding.

- Screen inbound co-investments and secondaries, and bring a view to the team. You run the first pass on what reaches us and form a position on it. What progresses is decided together with the Head of VC & Direct Investing and the wider team, so the value of your screen lies in the quality of the argument you bring to that conversation and in how sharply you separate the two or three worth our time from the rest.

- Run diligence on direct deals. The core of it is judgement on the business itself: how good the company is, how strong the founding team is, how large and how contested the market is, and whether the thesis survives contact with the evidence. The technical layer sits underneath, with cap table analysis, preference stacks and waterfalls, and pricing and NAV work on secondary positions, so we know exactly what we are buying and at what price. You will do this with support from senior members of the team, and contribute to primary fund diligence alongside the direct mandate.

- Author the investment memos that go to IC. The committee decides on what you put in front of it, so a memo with a gap in it, an inaccuracy, or a risk nobody spotted becomes a decision made on the wrong basis.

- Build the market view, and then the market position. Relationships with intermediaries, GPs and, over time, founders are what get us into constrained opportunities and keep us current on where secondaries are pricing. This part of the role grows as you do, and watching how competitors structure and go to market belongs to it, because that is what keeps us competitive on price.

- Help make the process repeatable. You will refine how we diligence direct deals and contribute to the sourcing, screening and monitoring tooling behind it, including AI-enabled approaches, so the volume we can handle is not capped by how much a person can read.

- Turn deals into something our clients can buy. The commercial team depends on this seat for qualified dealflow and for support packaging opportunities into investor-ready materials. Fund deployment runs at the pace this work sets.

The next Moonfarian: 

- Four or more years centred on venture and growth investing. That comes along one of two paths. Either direct investment expertise, sourcing and diligencing investments in technology companies at a venture capital, growth equity or crossover fund, or an allocator seat focused on VC and growth where you have underwritten co-investments hands-on. Directly relevant adjacent backgrounds include TMT and technology investment banking, tech-focused private equity or software buyout, corporate development or corporate VC at a technology company, and consulting with a tech or commercial diligence focus. What matters most is a demonstrable track record of hands-on deal work: screening opportunities, running diligence, and taking a view through to a decision.

- A network in venture you can already use. This one is non-negotiable. Relationships with GPs, intermediaries such as placement agents and bankers, and other LPs and co-investors, enough to get us access to constrained opportunities, support diligence and track spin-out candidates. You do not need the network of someone twice your experience. You do need a real one, and you will build a much larger one here.

- Investment judgement you can defend. You form a view on a company and argue it, including the case against. You can read a business and a founding team, size a market and test a thesis against what the evidence actually supports. You are genuinely fluent in emerging technology and can develop conviction on themes and business models, with AI front of mind but not the only lens. You assess attractiveness quickly on limited or imperfect information, you are comfortable with financial modelling and market analysis, and you know your way around cap tables, preference stacks and waterfalls, secondary pricing, VC term sheets and SPV mechanics. You can hold several live opportunities at once and prioritise sharply between them.

- An entrepreneurial instinct, which matters here as much as the investing. This one is non-negotiable too. This is a builder's seat as much as an investor's. You want a hand in structuring, go-to-market, process design and the operational scaffolding of a business line that is still being built. Your AI fluency goes past using the tools to designing processes around them.

- Communication that works in three different rooms, and relationships that outlast any one deal. You can pitch and tailor to an investment committee, to a commercial team, and to clients, and prepare the reports and presentations each of them needs. Just as important is what you build over time with GPs and intermediaries, the standing that makes them think of us when something scarce comes up, because that is what turns a contact list into access. Excellent written and spoken English is essential.

How the role is measured: 

- Deals sourced, screened, and taken through to IC.

- Timely deployment of Moonfare's proprietary funds, such as the Moonfare Technology Fund.

- Allocation secured with GPs and intermediaries, meaning access we would not otherwise have had.

- Whether IC can decide on your memos without rework, and whether risks surface in diligence rather than after close.

- Capital raised on direct deals and the performance ultimately generated. These are programme outcomes you contribute to rather than own alone, and they are read that way.

What success looks like: 

By six months, the deal pipeline runs without the Head of VC & Direct Investing having to chase it. Opportunities are screened as they arrive, you are bringing a formed view on each one to the team, and the queue is visible to everyone who needs it.|
By twelve months, deal review is fully operationalised, with a process the team can run rather than one person's habits, and more than ten direct deals have been through IC.

This role is unlikely to be a good match if you 

- Prefer to let relationships develop slowly and mostly in writing. Much of our access comes from conversations with managers and intermediaries you do not know yet, and someone reserved about starting them will find the sourcing half of this job hard going.

- Want a defined process to work inside. A good part of what this role runs does not exist yet, and you would be designing it while live deals are moving.

- Want sole authority over what you invest in. We discuss deals as a team and decide together what progresses, which means your view gets argued with before it gets acted on. If you want to run your own book without that, this will frustrate you.

What your growth could look like: 

The next step from here is Associate Principal. Getting there means leading the majority of diligence processes rather than running them with support, and having a network that generates opportunities rather than one that keeps you informed.

What you get here that you would not get at a fund: you join the Head of VC & Direct Investing in GP conversations from early on and inherit access to a built-up base of manager relationships. You see the commercial side of raising capital for a deal alongside the investment side, which most investors never touch. And you help build a wider business, across a discretionary fund, capital raising for individual deals and, in time, a secondary market.

If you feel you do not meet all of the requirements, we still encourage you to apply!

We can only accept applications from those eligible to live and work in Berlin/London. This is a hybrid role with office attendance required 4 days/week. 

Please note that we do not accept applications sent by email. You should submit your application directly through our careers website. 

Invest in Yourself: 

- Ownership and Impact: You are empowered to bring ideas, make decisions, and see your work directly contribute to Moonfare's success. 

- Transparent Environment: We believe in open communication. You will receive regular updates on company strategy, performance against our KPIs, and key business decisions. 

- Personal Growth: We support your development with an individual growth budget of €1,500 or 2% of your base salary (whichever is higher).

- Invest in Your Future: We support your long-term financial goals with a company pension scheme, providing a 20% employer contribution.

- Relax and Recharge: You start with 25 vacation days and you’ll receive one additional day for each year of tenure, up to a maximum of 30 days. Moonfare gifts two days during our annual end of year company shutdown.

- Daily Lunch: Enjoy a free lunch every day that you are in the Berlin office, with a weekly changing menu that includes salads, curries, pastas, and a variety of vegan and vegetarian options.

- Subsidised Public Transport: We support your commute with a monthly subsidy for the Deutschland job ticket, making your travel easier and more affordable.

- Fitness and Wellbeing: Stay active with a subsidised Urban Sports Club membership, giving you flexible access to a wide variety of sports and wellness activities across Germany.

- A Culture of Excellence: Join a team of ambitious, smart, and committed professionals who are passionate about revolutionising private market investing.

Your mission As our Application Security Engineer, you will play a key role in shaping and strengthening the security of our products and platforms. Working closely with highly skilled engineering, platform, and security teams, you will help build secure, resilient, and trusted software while driving a security-first culture across the organization. This is an opportunity to make a measurable impact on modern products, influence security strategy, and continuously develop your expertise in a collaborative and innovative environment.

- Drive product security across the entire software development lifecycle (SDLC).
- Perform threat modeling, architecture reviews, and security assessments for applications, APIs, and distributed systems.
- Identify, assess, prioritize, and support the remediation of security vulnerabilities.
- Integrate, operate, and continuously improve security tooling within CI/CD pipelines, including SAST, DAST, SCA, dependency scanning, and secrets-scanning solutions.
- Define, promote, and support secure coding standards and security best practices across engineering teams.
- Review and advise on authentication, authorization, identity management, secrets management, and service-to-service communication designs.
- Support penetration testing activities, conduct targeted security testing, and drive remediation efforts.
- Contribute to security policies, standards, and security awareness initiatives.
- Partner closely with software engineers, architects, and platform teams to embed security into development processes and strengthen our DevSecOps culture.

Your profile - 5+ years of experience in Product Security, Application Security, Software Security, Secure Software Development, or a related field.
- Strong understanding of secure software development practices and common application security vulnerabilities.
- Proven experience performing threat modeling, architecture reviews, code reviews, and application security assessments.
- Hands-on experience with SAST, DAST, SCA, dependency-scanning, and secrets-scanning tools.
- Strong knowledge of application security, API security, and distributed-system security.
- Experience securing authentication, authorization, and identity-related workflows.
- Solid understanding of OWASP, CWE, security testing methodologies, and modern security engineering practices.
- Experience working with CI/CD pipelines and applying DevSecOps principles.
- Ability to collaborate effectively with software engineering, platform, and DevOps teams.
- Fluent English skills are required; German language skills are a plus.
Nice to have 
- Development experience in C#, .NET, JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, or similar programming languages.
- Experience securing cloud-native applications and services in Azure and/or AWS environments.
- Relevant security certifications such as OSCP, CSSLP, OSWE, or GIAC Secure Development certifications.
- Experience working in agile software development environments.

Why us? Modernes, zentral gelegenes Büro: Nur 5 Gehminuten von der Haltestelle Bahrenfeld entfernt - bequeme Anreise garantiert!

Offene Unternehmenskultur: Tauche ein in ein internationales Arbeitsumfeld, in dem Ideen und Vielfalt gefördert werden.

Kollegiale Arbeitsatmosphäre: Genieße eine Arbeitsatmosphäre, die von Zusammenarbeit und Hands-on-Mentalität geprägt ist.

Hybrides Arbeitsmodell: Flexibilität - Kombiniere Arbeit vor Ort und im Home Office.

30 Tage Urlaub: Mehr Zeit für Erholung und Freizeit. Zusätzliche freie Tage am 24.12., 31.12. sowie einen halben Tag an deinem Geburtstag.

Attraktives Vergütungspaket: Wir honorieren deine Leistung angemessen.

- A solid understanding of data and technology topics: you speak the language of technical teams without needing to build solutions yourself
- Strong analytical and strategic thinking, combined with an entrepreneurial mindset
- A genuine consultant and service mindset
- Drive to deliver, initiative, and strong communication and teamwork skills
- A confident presence, paired with an independent, results-oriented way of working and a strong willingness to learn
- Very good MS Office skills
- Business-fluent command of German and English, both written and spoken

Look forward to: - Impact from Day One: A wide range of responsibilities with a high level of ownership and the opportunity to help shape processes, strategies, and products at the management level
- Culture & Team: A collaborative and supportive work environment in small, interdisciplinary teams with flat hierarchies, short decision-making paths, and a values-driven culture
- Exciting Environment: Innovative AI-focused projects and clients who are market leaders in their respective industries
- Growth: Individual opportunities for personal and professional development, along with targeted training and continuing education programs
- Benefits: Attractive compensation, regular team events (lunches, offsites), BusinessBike, corporate fitness (Wellpass), as well as free drinks, fruit, and snacks in the office
- Top Locations: A fantastic workplace right next to the English Garden in Munich or close to Alexanderplatz in Berlin

title: Software Engineer - Core Marketing Platforms
description:
THE POSITION 

Our roster has an opening with your name on it 

We're looking for a Software Engineer to join one of our Core Marketing Platforms teams , where you'll build and optimize high-performance microservices that power FanDuel's marketing ecosystem. You'll work on systems enabling critical capabilities such as real-time customer communications, personalized promotions, and targeted campaign delivery. 

Your work will focus on designing highly scalable, event-driven systems that process large volumes of real-time data, delivering intelligent insights to marketing partners. You'll help enable data-driven, personalized experiences for millions of customers across our platform. 

You'll work within a modern microservices and event-driven architecture, building Martech solutions enhanced by AI to drive customer engagement and retention. 

- Make existing systems simpler (e.g. by consolidating redundant systems, deleting unnecessary code, or removing/updating out of date documentation). 

- Solve well-defined problems independently, knowing when to seek input or guidance from the wider team 

- Translate technical designs into clean, well—tested code using appropriate technologies and current software engineering best practices, delivered on schedule.

- Contribute to team discussion on technical design, scoping and prioritisation. 

- Collaborate effectively across the team, surfacing risks and opportunities that arise from technical decisions. 

- Propose pragmatic solutions and share knowledge and learnings with the wider team. 

Everyone on our team has a part to play 

- You own parts of product and technology & strive to become a subject matter expert.  

- You write simple and extendable code following standards and best practices. 

- You help your team evolve by actively participating in the code review process, design discussions, team planning, and support ticket reviews.  

- You clearly document your software to ensure that future generations of developers understand the intention behind the features and components you build. 

- In the event of a problem, you can troubleshoot and identify a swift resolution. 

- You provide excellent customer support. 

- You estimate stories/tasks and deliver them on time. 

- Most importantly, you are humble, pragmatic, self-managed, thirsty for knowledge, never satisfied and always challenging the norm. Responsible for the state of the code you both inherit and produce  

- You participate in the on-call support rotation for your organization. 

What We’re Looking For 

What we’re looking for in our next teammate 

- Degree in Computer Science or related software engineering field, or equivalent practical experience. 2+ years of relevant work experience. 

- Strong backend experience with Java 

- Understanding of AWS as well as DevOps concepts such as IaC (we use Terraform) 

- Some experience with event streaming technologies such as SNS/SQS or Kafka. 

- Good grasp on relational, non-relational databases, messaging queues and handling concurrency. 

- Understanding of modern architectures, design patterns, and platform nuances 

- Appreciation of orchestration and containerisation, ideally Kubernetes 
(K8s) 

- Experience working with cloud-based infrastructure and technologies. 

- Experience with testing concepts, test tools, and integrating testing and best practices in the SDLC 

- Familiarity working in an Agile environment 

- Passion for working within a fast-paced environment and can adapt to change 

What You Can Expect 

- Interesting work - working in a fast-paced and ever-changing industry, new problems and exciting solutions are never too far away. There are always opportunities to learn new skills and broaden your horizons

- Belonging - everyone at FanDuel works for each other, we win together, make mistakes together and have lots of fun doing it.

FanDuel Group is the premier mobile gaming company in the United States and Canada. The company is based in New York with US offices in Los Angeles, Atlanta, and Jersey City, as well as global offices in Canada and Scotland. The company’s affiliates have offices worldwide, including in Ireland, Portugal, Romania, and Australia.

One is a multi-manager vehicle making primary fund investments into leading VC and growth managers across the US and Europe, where we have historically backed Founders Fund, a16z, Accel, Lightspeed, Khosla and General Catalyst. The other is the direct programme of co-investments and secondaries that those manager relationships generate, which is where this role's centre of gravity sits. You will report to the Head of VC & Direct Investing and work daily with the commercial team, who depend on you for qualified dealflow, and alongside Legal and Operations to close deals and launch the SPVs we distribute on the platform.

You will: 

- Own the direct deal pipeline. Everything from the moment an opportunity reaches us through to close is yours to run, so nothing sits unscreened and no access window quietly closes while we are still deciding.

- Screen inbound co-investments and secondaries, and bring a view to the team. You run the first pass on what reaches us and form a position on it. What progresses is decided together with the Head of VC & Direct Investing and the wider team, so the value of your screen lies in the quality of the argument you bring to that conversation and in how sharply you separate the two or three worth our time from the rest.

- Run diligence on direct deals. The core of it is judgement on the business itself: how good the company is, how strong the founding team is, how large and how contested the market is, and whether the thesis survives contact with the evidence. The technical layer sits underneath, with cap table analysis, preference stacks and waterfalls, and pricing and NAV work on secondary positions, so we know exactly what we are buying and at what price. You will do this with support from senior members of the team, and contribute to primary fund diligence alongside the direct mandate.

- Author the investment memos that go to IC. The committee decides on what you put in front of it, so a memo with a gap in it, an inaccuracy, or a risk nobody spotted becomes a decision made on the wrong basis.

- Build the market view, and then the market position. Relationships with intermediaries, GPs and, over time, founders are what get us into constrained opportunities and keep us current on where secondaries are pricing. This part of the role grows as you do, and watching how competitors structure and go to market belongs to it, because that is what keeps us competitive on price.

- Help make the process repeatable. You will refine how we diligence direct deals and contribute to the sourcing, screening and monitoring tooling behind it, including AI-enabled approaches, so the volume we can handle is not capped by how much a person can read.

- Turn deals into something our clients can buy. The commercial team depends on this seat for qualified dealflow and for support packaging opportunities into investor-ready materials. Fund deployment runs at the pace this work sets.

The next Moonfarian: 

- Four or more years centred on venture and growth investing. That comes along one of two paths. Either direct investment expertise, sourcing and diligencing investments in technology companies at a venture capital, growth equity or crossover fund, or an allocator seat focused on VC and growth where you have underwritten co-investments hands-on. Directly relevant adjacent backgrounds include TMT and technology investment banking, tech-focused private equity or software buyout, corporate development or corporate VC at a technology company, and consulting with a tech or commercial diligence focus. What matters most is a demonstrable track record of hands-on deal work: screening opportunities, running diligence, and taking a view through to a decision.

- A network in venture you can already use. This one is non-negotiable. Relationships with GPs, intermediaries such as placement agents and bankers, and other LPs and co-investors, enough to get us access to constrained opportunities, support diligence and track spin-out candidates. You do not need the network of someone twice your experience. You do need a real one, and you will build a much larger one here.

- Investment judgement you can defend. You form a view on a company and argue it, including the case against. You can read a business and a founding team, size a market and test a thesis against what the evidence actually supports. You are genuinely fluent in emerging technology and can develop conviction on themes and business models, with AI front of mind but not the only lens. You assess attractiveness quickly on limited or imperfect information, you are comfortable with financial modelling and market analysis, and you know your way around cap tables, preference stacks and waterfalls, secondary pricing, VC term sheets and SPV mechanics. You can hold several live opportunities at once and prioritise sharply between them.

- An entrepreneurial instinct, which matters here as much as the investing. This one is non-negotiable too. This is a builder's seat as much as an investor's. You want a hand in structuring, go-to-market, process design and the operational scaffolding of a business line that is still being built. Your AI fluency goes past using the tools to designing processes around them.

- Communication that works in three different rooms, and relationships that outlast any one deal. You can pitch and tailor to an investment committee, to a commercial team, and to clients, and prepare the reports and presentations each of them needs. Just as important is what you build over time with GPs and intermediaries, the standing that makes them think of us when something scarce comes up, because that is what turns a contact list into access. Excellent written and spoken English is essential.

How the role is measured: 

- Deals sourced, screened, and taken through to IC.

- Timely deployment of Moonfare's proprietary funds, such as the Moonfare Technology Fund.

- Allocation secured with GPs and intermediaries, meaning access we would not otherwise have had.

- Whether IC can decide on your memos without rework, and whether risks surface in diligence rather than after close.

- Capital raised on direct deals and the performance ultimately generated. These are programme outcomes you contribute to rather than own alone, and they are read that way.

What success looks like: 

By six months, the deal pipeline runs without the Head of VC & Direct Investing having to chase it. Opportunities are screened as they arrive, you are bringing a formed view on each one to the team, and the queue is visible to everyone who needs it.|
By twelve months, deal review is fully operationalised, with a process the team can run rather than one person's habits, and more than ten direct deals have been through IC.

This role is unlikely to be a good match if you 

- Prefer to let relationships develop slowly and mostly in writing. Much of our access comes from conversations with managers and intermediaries you do not know yet, and someone reserved about starting them will find the sourcing half of this job hard going.

- Want a defined process to work inside. A good part of what this role runs does not exist yet, and you would be designing it while live deals are moving.

- Want sole authority over what you invest in. We discuss deals as a team and decide together what progresses, which means your view gets argued with before it gets acted on. If you want to run your own book without that, this will frustrate you.

What your growth could look like: 

The next step from here is Associate Principal. Getting there means leading the majority of diligence processes rather than running them with support, and having a network that generates opportunities rather than one that keeps you informed.

What you get here that you would not get at a fund: you join the Head of VC & Direct Investing in GP conversations from early on and inherit access to a built-up base of manager relationships. You see the commercial side of raising capital for a deal alongside the investment side, which most investors never touch. And you help build a wider business, across a discretionary fund, capital raising for individual deals and, in time, a secondary market.

If you feel you do not meet all of the requirements, we still encourage you to apply!

The Ledger Platform team owns the ledger across all of iwoca's products, from credit cards to our lending range, plus everything around it: reconciliation, financial reporting, and the data Finance, Accounting and Capital Markets run on. The role 

Responsibility and Autonomy:

- Lead the delivery of projects involving many stakeholders and systems.

- Go beyond the code to develop deep expertise in our domain — our core financial products and our stakeholders' needs — and become a trusted technical advisor to the business.

- Perform detailed technical scoping and prototyping to support feasibility testing and decision making.

Delivery and Collaboration

- Use domain modelling to find the simple design behind a complicated problem, and structure software so that it is easy to understand, test and evolve.

- Be pragmatic about which parts of a problem actually need solving now. The hardest work here is deciding what not to build.

The company 

Imagine a world where every small business has the power to thrive. That's the world we're building at iwoca. Senior Software Engineer - Customer Operations Platform 

Hybrid in London, UK

We’re looking for a Senior Software Engineer 

iwoca’s operational tools and processes are a competitive advantage, allowing us to give great customer service, manage risk, and get money into our customers’ hands as quickly as possible.

You’ll join our growing Customer Operations Platform team to help improve the systems that power these processes, building tailored flows for our Operations teams, automating processes using AI, using ML models to make smarter decisions, and improving the reliability of our communication services.

The company 

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The role 

As a Senior Engineer you’ll run projects end to end, work out what' s actually needed, design it, build it and look after it in production.

- Take the lead on complex projects that span many systems and many stakeholders — e.g. CRM, telephony, contact, and task management

description:
About Us 

Perk (formerly TravelPerk) is the intelligent platform for travel and spend management. Built to tackle the time-consuming, manual work that gets in the way of real work, our tools automate everything from travel bookings to expenses, invoice processing, and more. By eliminating this shadow work that wastes hours, erodes morale, and saps innovation, we're on a mission to power real work, with real impact.

We're trusted by more than 12,000 companies worldwide, including Bolt, GoCardless, and Fabletics, and we're tackling the 7 hours of lost productivity per employee each week, a $1.7 trillion problem .

Founded in 2015, Perk has grown into a global company of more than 1,800 people across 12 offices globally, with headquarters in London and Boston. We combine innovation, control, and simplicity to transform how businesses work and how people feel at work.

At Perk, we're driven by our values, like being an owner, delivering a 7-star experience, and working as one team. We value curiosity, purpose, and mindset, not just knowledge, to unlock the power in your potential. Our talent team brings together leading minds from the travel, fintech, and SaaS industries, representing over 70 countries. If you're excited about having a real impact and shaping how millions of people experience work, we'd love you on the team.

Visit www.perk.com to learn more.

About the role: 

As our Account Management team grows we are looking for a customer-oriented and result-driven Enterprise AM to join us.

As an Enterprise Account Manager you will be actively contributing to our continued customer satisfaction as well as working to increase growth and margin within existing accounts.

In this role you will be responsible for a portfolio of top accounts. You must possess a genuine hunger to navigate your accounts in a fast-changing, hyper-growth environment, be ready to roll-up your sleeves and work hard.

What You’ll Do 

- Own a portfolio of Tier 1 customers, building trusted relationships with champions, key decision makers, and executive stakeholders across Finance, Procurement, Travel, HR, IT, and Leadership.

- Build and execute strategic account plans by developing a deep understanding of your customers' business, identifying expansion opportunities, mitigating risks, and maximising long-term customer value.

- Identify growth opportunities across business units, geographies, and product lines to expand your portfolio through new business opportunities, upselling, and cross-selling.

- Drive adoption across Perk's Travel and Spend platform by identifying underutilised features, expanding use cases, and partnering with customers on change management initiatives.

- Leverage data and analytics to lead Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs), delivering reports and presentations that demonstrate business outcomes, product adoption, ROI, and future strategic opportunities to senior stakeholders.

- Be an expert across Perk's Travel and Spend platform to educate customers on new capabilities and consistently meet or exceed quarterly expansion targets.

- Identify common challenges within each account, develop timely solutions, and implement long-term strategies that improve customer outcomes and satisfaction.

- Be Perk's biggest advocate within your customers and your customers' biggest advocate within Perk by partnering with Product, Engineering, and Technical Support teams to resolve issues, influence product improvements, and represent the voice of the customer.

- Effectively prioritise your time and resources to maximise impact across your portfolio and key business initiatives.

What We're Looking For 

- Significant experience managing a portfolio of Tier 1 customers in a SaaS, travel-tech, fintech, or spend management environment. Experience working with finance, procurement, travel, or expense management ecosystems is a strong plus.

- Proven ability to build relationships across Finance, Procurement, Travel, HR, IT, and executive leadership within large enterprise organisations.

- Experience navigating complex enterprise organisations with multiple stakeholders, procurement processes, and executive decision-makers.

- Outstanding presentation and communication skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders at all levels and build trusted, long-term relationships.

- Strong financial, commercial, and analytical acumen, with the ability to discuss T&E policy, spend controls, ROI, cost optimisation, and operational efficiency with finance leaders.

- Results-oriented mindset with a strong focus on customer satisfaction and long-term customer value.

- Excellent prioritisation and time management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities across a portfolio of strategic accounts.

On top of that, you will only be the right candidate if you are: 

- Empathetic: someone who can identify with the customer and genuinely wants to support them using an optimal problem-solving methodology

- Honest, open and trustworthy: your peers and managers can trust you. You are a team player, don’t play political games, and care more about the team’s success than about your own career gains

- Focused and determined: You don’t let yourself be distracted. You can focus on accomplishing big wins and never get lost in less important ideas that are floating around

- Growth Mindset: You seek feedback early and often and are open to both give and take constructive and direct criticism

- Experience using inside sales tools like Salesforce, Google Tools, Zendesk, Looker.

What We Offer 

- Receive competitive compensation and equity ownership in Perk

- Rest and recharge with 25 days of annual leave plus bank holidays

- Take control of your physical health with private medical cover and voluntary dental insurance from Bupa, and discounted gym memberships with GymFlex

- Plan for your future with our qualifying earnings company pension plan with Aviva

- Know that your loved ones are protected financially through your Life Insurance if the worst were to happen

- Rest assured that you’re covered by income protection in case you experience a long-term sickness or absence

- Leverage tax-efficient cycle and electric car schemes with Cycle2Work & Octopus

- Join our unforgettable Perk events, including our spectacular annual summer party

- Always feel supported with Spring Health, our market-leading wellbeing partner, providing fast, comprehensive access to 12x therapy and 12x coaching sessions for you and your loved ones

- Focus on your family with 12-16 weeks’ paid parental leave

- Contribute to your community with 16 paid hours per year to spend volunteering for your dearest charitable causes

- Broaden your horizons with up to 20 "Work from Anywhere" days per year

- Stay savvy with access to a wide variety of discounts and rewards

- Follow your passions and take a four-week, fully paid sabbatical once you reach 5 years

- Let us help you move to one of our hubs with relocation support

AI at Perk 
AI is embedded in how we work across every function. The tools you'll use day-to-day are AI-enabled so you can move faster and spend more time on the work that matters. In practice, that means using AI to research and prioritise accounts, draft and refine outreach, handle customer interactions more effectively, synthesise information, and cut through shadow work - the invisible tasks that pull people away from the work only they can do - so you can focus on relationships and outcomes.

How We Work 

At Perk, we take an IRL-first approach to work, where our team works together in-person 3 days a week. As such, this role requires you to be based within commuting distance of our hubs. We fundamentally believe in the value of meeting in real life to improve connectivity, productivity, creativity and ultimately making us a great place to work.

For certain roles, we can help with relocation from anywhere in the world, English is the official language at the office. Please submit your resume in English if you choose to apply. Do not forget to submit an updated portfolio and/or resume.

Perk is a global company with a diverse customer base, and we want to make sure the people behind our product reflect that. We’re an equal opportunity employer, which means you’re welcome at Perk regardless of how you look, where you’re from, or anything else that makes you, well, you.

Protect Yourself from Recruitment Scams 

All official communication from Perk will always come from email addresses ending in @ perk.com or @ externalperk.com , our verified social media channels, or recruiters listed on our official LinkedIn page. We will never ask you to pay for equipment, training, or fees, request sensitive personal information such as bank details early in the process, or communicate through unofficial apps like WhatsApp, Telegram, or Signal. If you receive a message claiming to be from Perk that seems suspicious, please do not respond. Forward it to security [at] perk .com , and we will confirm whether it is legitimate.

title: Team Lead, Account Development Representatives
description:
Are you ready to unlock intelligence? 

If you don’t think you meet all of the criteria below but are still interested in the job, please apply. Nobody checks every box - we’re looking for candidates that are particularly strong in a few areas, and have some interest and capabilities in others.

About the Role: 

Kong is hiring an ADR Team Lead to support our NEMEA region: the UK, Benelux, and Nordics. This is a player-coach role. You'll carry your own pipeline targets while taking an active hand in developing the team around you, especially the newer ADRs still finding their footing.

You'll work closely with, and report into, the Senior Manager for NEMEA. You're shaping how the team operates, not running it solo. Think of this as a high-impact individual contributor role with a leadership layer built in: the natural next step for an ADR who's ready to start making other people better, not just themselves.

Our NEMEA team is already strong. Driven, independent, hitting their numbers. What they need isn't more oversight. They need someone who sharpens how the team works, especially around process and tooling, while making sure newer reps get the support to ramp fast.

You'll report to Oscar Winberg. He moves fast, sets a high bar, and expects people to bring solutions, not just flag problems. He's direct, so you'll always know exactly where you stand, and he expects that same directness back: if you disagree, he wants the pushback, backed by data, not silence. Earn his trust and he'll hand you real ownership. What he won't do is hand-hold, so this role suits someone who'd rather be given room to run than told exactly what to do.

What You'll Do: 

Carry your own number. You'll hit your own pipeline targets as an active ADR. Your activity and results set the standard for everyone watching. You'll contribute to weekly forecasting alongside the Senior Manager.

Support newer ADRs. You'll be the first point of contact for less tenured reps, helping them ramp faster and build good habits early. You'll help with onboarding alongside the Senior Manager and Enablement, and run regular 1:1s with newer ADRs. Different reps need different things from you, so you'll read where each person is and adjust your coaching accordingly rather than running the same playbook on everyone. You'll help build individual development plans grounded in a real read of each rep's attitude, process, and results, and you'll flag underperformance early, with context, instead of letting it fester.

Coach and upskill the team. You'll support team coaching sessions: live dialling, pitch practice, feedback loops. You'll run or contribute to upskilling initiatives, on your own or with Enablement. You'll share what's working, best practices, sequences, outbound approaches, with the wider team, and give direct, specific feedback often, recognizing strong work and not letting bad habits slide.

Sharpen process and tooling. You'll help spot where the team's workflows and tooling could run more efficiently, and support the Senior Manager in rolling out improvements without stripping reps of their autonomy. You'll be the go-to person for best practice on Salesforce, Outreach, and the team's automation tools.

Contribute to the wider GTM motion. You'll keep strong alignment with your AE partners and take part in pipe review cadences. You'll support the Senior Manager in preparing performance updates and regional insights, and join bi-weekly RD cadences where it makes sense.

What You'll Bring: 

- Hands-on ADR or SDR experience. You know what this job feels like from the inside, not just what it looks like from a deck.

- A real coach's instinct. You get energy from making other people better, not just from hitting your own number.

- The ability to juggle competing priorities without dropping the ball. Your own quota, coaching newer reps, and process work will all pull on your time in the same week, and you know how to decide what actually matters right now.

- Strong time management. This is one we screen for directly, not something we assume comes with experience.

- A bias for building. You spot what needs fixing and go build it, rather than working only through a list of tasks someone else handed you.

- Analytical rigor. You make calls based on data, not gut feel, and you're comfortable being specific about why a number moved, including when that number is going the wrong way.

- You touch the line. Your metrics back it up: leading indicators (activity, sequence execution, pipeline hygiene) and lagging indicators (quota attainment, pipeline generated) that show a track record of real discipline, not one good quarter.

- Real trust with your AE and RD partners, earned through consistency, not just alignment on paper.

- Transparency, especially with leadership, especially when something isn't on track. We'd rather hear it early than find out later.

- The kind of presence the team actually looks up to, not just reports to.

- Comfort in an allbound model with a heavy outbound emphasis.

- Self-awareness and a genuine investment in growing as a leader.

- Language skills relevant to the UK, Benelux, or Nordics are a bonus, not a requirement.

We'll consider strong internal and external candidates. For external hires, the bar is high: we're looking for someone who brings something genuinely differentiated.

Culture and Values: 

The EMEA SDR team are weather makers. We don't wait for opportunity, we create it. We're accountable, relentless, and we invest in each other like no other team does.

About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

- ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

- ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

- ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

- High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

- Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

- AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

- Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

- Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

- Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

- Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

- Learning & development : ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

- Social travel : We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

- Co-working : If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role 

We're looking for a Data Scientist - Product Analytics to join our Growth Data team. You'll own the analysis behind how people discover, adopt and stick with ElevenLabs' products, partnering closely with Product, Growth and the central Data team's certified metrics layer.

- Define and own product health metrics: activation, feature adoption, retention and engagement across ElevenCreative, ElevenAgents and ElevenAPI.

- Design, analyse and communicate the results of product experiments (A/B tests, feature launches, onboarding changes).

- Partner with Analytics Engineering on the certified product KPI layer in dbt, and with Product on turning ambiguous questions into trusted analysis.

- Work alongside fellow Growth data scientists on marketing- and revenue-adjacent questions that touch the product funnel.

Requirements 

Demonstrated experience as a data scientist embedded with a product or growth team, ideally at a product-led company.

- Strong SQL and Python , with hands-on experience in experimentation (A/B testing) and product analytics.

- Ability to translate ambiguous product questions into clear, reusable analysis and defensible metrics.

- Comfort working directly with Product and Growth stakeholders , and pushing back on ill-defined asks.

- Structured thinker who can move fast without sacrificing rigour.

Bonus 

- Experience with activation / retention modelling or lifecycle analytics at a consumer or prosumer product.

- Experience with dbt or a modern warehouse, partnering directly with analytics engineers.

- Experience using AI tools or agents to speed up analysis or enable self-serve data access.

Growth potential 

We believe in hiring the best talent in the world to make an impact in the right role at the right time. At ElevenLabs, strong performance creates opportunities for growth. Here are some of the career paths you can expect after excelling in this role:

- Grow into a Senior or Staff Product Data Scientist role as the Growth Data team scales.

description:
Building the Future of Open Finance 

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

Before you apply, we encourage you to explore our culture page to understand what drives us and how we work.

The team 

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

Kraken’s Consumer Creative & Design team owns end-to-end creative execution for Kraken Consumer and Krak. Our disciplines cover performance ad creative, 2D and 3D design, motion design, AI video creative and web design, turning growth strategy into creative that converts across paid, owned and organic surfaces. We work closely with Product Marketing, Performance Marketing, Content & Social, Lifecycle and our regional leads, holding the line on brand and messaging quality on everything that ships.

The opportunity 

Great creative starts with a sharp idea, and the earlier it arrives, the better the work gets. As our Creative Strategist & Producer, you bring ideas in at the start of a campaign and you can also make them. Up to half the role is writing complete, concept-led briefs for paid static and motion, and sometimes organic and social, then briefing them into our creatives and designers. The other half is making work yourself, in whatever format you’re strongest at. You also help Product Marketing and Performance Marketing write stronger briefs of their own.

This role is for a proactive self-starter. Nobody will hand you the idea: you go and find it, pitch it and get it made.

You report to the Creative Lead, Consumer Creative & Design, who gives you direction, feedback and cover in reviews. This is an individual contributor role with no direct reports. You work daily with Product Marketing and Performance Marketing, who bring deep knowledge of the product and the media channels, and with the creatives who bring your briefs to life.

- Spot opportunities in culture every day. Watch pop culture, trends, competitors, comments and performance data, and turn what you find into ideas we ship the same week. Stay close to financial markets and to Kraken’s audience.

- Write complete, concept-led briefs for paid static and motion, built with Product Marketing and Performance Marketing, and brief them into the performance creatives and designers.

- Help Product Marketing and Performance Marketing managers sharpen their own briefs, bringing the concept, the hook and the cultural angle to the start of the process.

- Pitch original concepts for paid and social before anyone asks, so ideas reach the team already sharp.

- Make your own content for paid and organic. The format is open: you could be a meme machine, an AI video specialist, someone who performs to camera, or something we haven’t thought of. What matters is that it feels native to the feed and ships fast.

- Use performance data and social listening as creative input, and get more distinct angles into tests each month.Performance Marketing owns test design and readouts; you own the creative response.

- React inside the news cycle. You spot the moment, and you brief it or make it yourself.

- Partner with Product Marketing and compliance to get work approved without losing the idea.

- Keep your briefs and files clean enough for other people to build on.

What you bring 

- 5+ years in creative strategy, social, content or performance creative at a high-volume in-house team, brand or agency, ideally in fintech, crypto, gaming or another regulated category.

- A portfolio submitted with your application. Include two or three concept-led briefs or concept decks, with what shipped and how it performed where you’re able to share it, plus work you made yourself in the formats that are your strength. Include one idea you spotted in culture or data and took to market, with a short note on what the results told you and what you changed.

- A proactive, self-starting way of working. You find the idea, pitch it and drive it to be shipped without waiting to be asked, and you’re comfortable owning your workflow with light direction.

- Pop-culture fluency and a chronically online persona, with comedic instinct and a sense for what’s about to feel dated.

- A performance marketer’s grip on what a good brief needs: a clear objective, audience, hook, platform, format and set of constraints, and the ability to coach others toward it.

- A creative superpower you can execute on alone, with shipped work to show for it.

- Platform-native instincts across Meta, TikTok, YouTube, Reddit and X. You can explain why the same idea needs a different build on each one.

- Fluency in the metrics creative moves, and the habit of using performance data and social listening as inputs to ideas.

- A solid copywriting instinct. Plain language, value first, no hype and no jargon.

- Comfort working inside regulatory constraints, with concepts that survive risk warnings and market-specific requirements.

- Speed without sloppiness. Comfortable with fast turnarounds, several review rounds and late changes.

description:
