title: Senior Enterprise Customer Success Manager
description:
About Pleo 

Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’.

The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years.

Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.

About the role 

We’re looking for a Senior Enterprise Customer Success Manager to join our Customer Experience team at Pleo. In this role, you’ll own a portfolio of large, complex, and strategically important enterprise customers, helping them achieve measurable business outcomes, expand adoption, manage change, and build long-term value with Pleo.

You’ll serve as a trusted advisor to senior customer stakeholders while coordinating the broader Pleo relationship across Customer Success, Product, Support, Sales, Finance, and other internal teams.

This is not a reactive account-management role. You’ll be expected to understand each customer’s business priorities, operating model, success criteria, and risk profile. You’ll turn that understanding into clear success plans, executive engagement strategies, adoption programs, renewal plans, and growth opportunities.

The right candidate will bring at least three years of direct experience managing enterprise customers , along with the communication skills, commercial judgment, and operational discipline required to manage high-value relationships in a fast-paced technology environment.

Who you’ll be working with and reporting to 

You’ll report to our Manager of Customer Success, Large & High-Growth Customers and work closely with teams across:

- Customer Support

- Customer Onboarding

- Sales and Account Management

- Product and Product Operations

- Revenue Operations

- Finance

- Data and Analytics

- Program Management and Operations

You’ll work with customer stakeholders across finance, procurement, operations, technology, transformation, and executive leadership.

You’ll be responsible for creating alignment across these stakeholders, establishing clear governance, and ensuring Pleo remains connected to the customer’s evolving strategic and operational priorities.

What you’ll be doing 

As a Senior Enterprise Customer Success Manager , you will:

- Own a portfolio of enterprise customers with accountability for customer health, value realisation, adoption, retention, renewal readiness, advocacy, and growth.

- Build trusted relationships with senior and executive stakeholders , positioning yourself as a credible advisor who understands their business priorities and operating environment.

- Develop detailed customer success plans that connect the customer’s strategic goals to measurable outcomes, adoption milestones, responsibilities, and timelines.

- Lead executive business reviews and strategic customer meetings that demonstrate value, address risks, align stakeholders, and create clear next steps.

- Drive product adoption across complex customer organisations , helping customers expand usage across teams, entities, locations, use cases, and workflows.

- Create and maintain detailed stakeholder maps , identifying decision-makers, champions, influencers, operational contacts, blockers, and executive sponsors.

- Identify churn risk early using product usage, engagement, stakeholder, support, financial, organisational, and external business signals.

- Build and execute churn-prevention plans with clear actions, owners, timelines, customer commitments, and executive escalation paths.

- Maintain detailed and accurate forecasts across renewals, risk, customer health, expected outcomes, growth opportunities, and major account milestones.

- Lead renewal-readiness activities by ensuring customer value is documented, risks are addressed, stakeholders are aligned, and commercial partners have accurate account intelligence.

- Identify and support expansion opportunities by connecting additional Pleo capabilities, products, or use cases to the customer’s evolving business needs.

- Coordinate complex customer escalations across Support, Product, Engineering, Finance, and other teams while maintaining clear and confident customer communication.

- Act as the customer’s internal advocate , ensuring customer needs, feedback, risks, and opportunities are visible to the right stakeholders at Pleo.

- Navigate customer change effectively , including leadership transitions, reorganisations, acquisitions, market expansion, platform changes, and evolving business priorities.

- Track customer commitments and outcomes with strong operational discipline, ensuring actions are documented, owned, and completed.

- Contribute to the evolution of Pleo’s enterprise Customer Success model by sharing best practices, customer insights, playbooks, and recommendations.

- Support peer development and knowledge sharing across the Customer Success team without holding direct people-management responsibility.

To put things into context 

In this role, you can expect to work on priorities such as:

- strengthening relationships with Pleo’s largest and most strategic customers

- improving enterprise customer retention and renewal predictability

- increasing adoption across complex customer organisations

- creating stronger executive engagement and governance

- identifying churn risk before it becomes a renewal issue

- improving forecast accuracy and account visibility

- coordinating complex customer needs across multiple internal teams

- helping customers quantify and communicate the value they receive from Pleo

- identifying opportunities for expansion and deeper product adoption

- improving the consistency and quality of enterprise success planning

- helping customers navigate operational and organisational change

- turning customer feedback into actionable Product and CX insight

You can expect to work across a technology environment that includes CRM, Customer Success platforms, support systems, product analytics, business intelligence tools, workflow tools, and collaboration platforms .

Examples may include Vitally, Gainsight or similar, Zendesk, Looker, Tableau or Power BI, Jira, Asana, and Slack.

What you bring 

You’ll thrive in this role if you have:

- At least three years of direct enterprise Customer Success or strategic account-management experience , managing large, complex, and high-value B2B customers.

- Five or more years of overall experience in Customer Success, account management, consulting, implementation, or a related customer-facing role.

- Experience working in SaaS, fintech, enterprise technology, or another complex B2B technology environment .

- A proven record of retaining and growing enterprise customers , including managing renewals, adoption, risk, and value realisation.

- Strong executive relationship-management skills , with the confidence and credibility to engage senior decision-makers and business leaders.

- Experience managing complex stakeholder environments involving multiple teams, business units, regions, entities, or decision-makers.

- Strong churn-prediction and prevention skills , including the ability to interpret customer signals, identify root causes, and build effective recovery plans.

- Detailed forecasting experience across renewals, customer risk, account health, adoption, and expansion opportunities.

- Strong commercial judgment , with an understanding of how customer outcomes connect to retention, revenue, expansion, and long-term account value.

- Excellent verbal and written communication skills , including the ability to lead difficult conversations, present to executives, and simplify complex issues.

- Experience building strategic success plans, account plans, stakeholder maps, and executive business reviews .

- Strong analytical skills , with the ability to interpret customer data, product usage, service trends, and business information.

- Strong cross-functional leadership skills , with the ability to align internal stakeholders without relying on direct authority.

- A structured and proactive approach to account management , with excellent follow-through and attention to detail.

- Comfort working in a fast-paced growth environment where customer expectations, internal priorities, and business needs can evolve quickly.

- The ability to balance strategic relationship management with detailed operational execution .

Nice to have 

- Experience in fintech, payments, spend management, financial operations, or expense-management technology

- Experience working with finance leaders, procurement teams, controllers, CFO organisations, or transformation leaders

- Experience managing multi-country or multinational enterprise customers

- Familiarity with ERP, accounting, procurement, or financial-system integrations

- Experience supporting customers through significant organisational or technology transformation

- Exposure to AI-enabled Customer Success, predictive health models, automated risk detection, or digital engagement

- Experience partnering with Product teams on strategic customer feedback and roadmap discussions

- Experience managing accounts with complex security, compliance, governance, or implementation requirements

Why is this role a good fit for you? 

This role is a good fit for you if:

- You enjoy building strategic relationships with complex enterprise customers.

- You are comfortable engaging senior leaders and navigating high-stakes customer situations.

- You know how to connect product adoption to measurable customer outcomes.

- You are proactive about identifying and addressing churn risk.

- You combine strong relationship skills with rigorous account-management discipline.

- You are confident leading executive reviews, renewal discussions, and difficult customer conversations.

- You enjoy coordinating internal teams around complex customer needs.

- You want direct responsibility for protecting and growing some of Pleo’s most important customer relationships.

This role is not a good fit for you if: 

- You have not directly managed enterprise or strategic customer relationships.

- You prefer transactional or high-volume customer portfolios.

- You are uncomfortable owning customer risk, retention, and renewal readiness.

- You prefer reacting to customer requests rather than building proactive engagement strategies.

- You are uncomfortable engaging executive stakeholders or leading difficult conversations.

- You do not enjoy detailed forecasting, CRM management, and account planning.

- You prefer working independently without significant cross-functional coordination.

- You are looking for a people-management role rather than a senior individual-contributor position.

How you’ll develop in this role 

In your first 1 month at Pleo, you’ll: 

- Learn Pleo’s product, enterprise customer journey, value proposition, and Customer Success operating model.

- Build a detailed understanding of your customer portfolio, including revenue, renewal dates, usage, stakeholders, open issues, risks, and growth potential.

- Establish relationships with key customer stakeholders and internal ac

title: Graduate Deployment Strategist
description:
TL;DR: Our graduate roles are about who we believe you can become, not your previous experiences and qualifications. Everyone has to take the first step somewhere and we’re excited about creating this environment. 

You'll walk into some of the world's most complex enterprise systems and deploy Conduct against the challenges our customers face. You build the kind of trust that turns an initial pilot into a long-term partnership - and the product insights you bring back will directly shape what we build next.

Why Conduct 

We believe the world's largest companies should move at the speed of their ideas, not the speed of the decade-old systems they run on. Today they don't.

Every process change, every new product line runs into SAP systems layered with decades of custom code and complexity no human mind can fully comprehend. New requirements take months to ship, system migrations cost $100M+ and years of pain.

We're building the AI operating system that absorbs this complexity and gives enterprises back their speed and ambition. Major enterprises already trust us with their most critical systems, we've closed game-changing SI partnerships, just raised a $60M Series A, and demand is outpacing what we can service.

We're a small, talent-dense team doing our life's work out of London and NYC. Extreme ownership, high velocity, low-ego collaboration. What you build here shapes the company and how the world's largest companies operate. We sponsor visas and are convinced diverse teams build better products, so we especially encourage underrepresented groups in tech to reach out.

What you'll own 

You will make sure Conduct lands and sticks. You join strategic accounts early, run the technical deployment hands-on, and fully take over post-sale.

No two days look the same: you fly out to customers when it counts, you onboard hundreds of end users, surface expansion signals, and eventually turn a single entry point into a multi-year partnership.

Most importantly, you will have a direct line into product and shape Conduct’s product roadmap as we further build out the platform.

This is a very entrepreneurial role, our GTM team is still small and lean. You'll build the engine behind everything: onboarding flows, tooling, reusable playbooks — enough that customer capacity compounds without headcount scaling linearly.

Who we hire 

We're looking for sharp, driven, high potential graduates who share our obsession with understanding how software works.

You'll fit right in if your peers describe you are one of the sharpest people they have met, you’re hungry to work at pace and at your best in an environment which intersects technical and commercial enterprise.

description:
Your wellbeing, our mission. Join a company shaping a healthier world. 

GET TO KNOW US 

At Wellhub we're revolutionizing workplace wellness. Our platform connects employees worldwide to the best partners for fitness, mindfulness, therapy, nutrition, and sleep—all in one simple subscription. Headquartered in NYC with team members in Europe, North America and South America, we’re on a mission to make every company a wellness company.

We believe work should be fulfilling, inspiring, and balanced. Here, you’ll find a team that values wellbeing, collaboration, and different perspectives, where passion and creativity push boundaries to create real impact. Your contributions will help shape a healthier, more balanced world for you and millions of people globally. 

Join us in redefining the future of wellbeing! 

THE OPPORTUNITY 

We are hiring a Senior Enterprise Client Success Manager to join our Client Success team in London.

Client Success at Wellhub plays a critical role in ensuring our largest and most strategic enterprise clients successfully adopt, scale, and extract measurable value from our wellbeing solutions. In this role, you will manage a portfolio of complex enterprise accounts, owning the post-sale relationship and driving client retention, engagement, and commercial outcomes.

This is a hands-on, client-facing role suited for someone who is comfortable managing complexity, building strong stakeholder relationships, and working cross-functionally to deliver impact. The role is hybrid, with an expectation to be in the office 2x per week.

YOUR IMPACT 

- Own the post-sale lifecycle for a portfolio of large enterprise clients, acting as the primary point of contact and ensuring long-term partnership success.

- Build and maintain trusted relationships with HR, Reward, and Wellbeing stakeholders across complex client organisations.

- Drive client adoption, engagement, and retention by translating client goals into clear success and engagement plans.

- Lead renewals and support expansion opportunities within your portfolio, clearly articulating value and impact.

- Use data and insights to monitor performance, identify risks, and recommend improvements to client strategy.

- Collaborate closely with internal teams (Wellbeing Engagement, Operations, Customer Experience, User Growth, Partnerships, Commercial) to ensure effective delivery.

- Proactively identify issues and risks, clearly articulating client impact and urgency to your manager to enable timely escalation and resolution.

WHO YOU ARE

- 8+ years of experience in Client Success, Account Management, or a similar client-facing role.

- Experience managing mid-to-large enterprise clients in a complex, fast-paced environment.

- Comfortable owning renewals and participating in commercial conversations with clients.

- Strong relationship-building skills, with the ability to engage and influence senior client stakeholders.

- Data-aware, with confidence using insights and reporting to inform decisions and conversations.

- Highly organised, able to manage multiple accounts and priorities simultaneously.

- A collaborative, resilient professional who remains calm and solution-oriented when navigating change and complexity.

We recognize that individuals approach job applications differently. We strongly encourage all aspiring applicants to go for it, even if they don't match the job description 100%. We welcome your application and will be delighted to explore if you could be a great fit for our team. For this specific role, please note that prior experience in driving new business growth and successfully securing significant contracts with complex organizations are mandatory requirements.

WHAT WE OFFER YOU 

With thoughtful benefits, emotional wellbeing resources, and a culture that empowers you to take ownership of your role and your wellbeing, we create an environment where you can thrive in all dimensions of your life. Our benefits include:

WELLHUB: Free Gold membership with access to onsite gyms and studios, digital fitness programs, and online wellness resources for meditation, nutrition, mental wellbeing support, and more! Add up to three family members to your plan, ensuring access to wellness for those who matter most to you.

HEALTHCARE: Health and dental insurance. 

FLEXIBLE WORK: As a Flexible First company, we offer hybrid and remote options to give you the freedom to work in a way that suits you. The model for this specific role can be discussed with your recruiter and hiring manager. We offer all employees a one-time reimbursement to set up their home office equipment and a monthly work allowance to help cover the costs of working from home. Our offices are in Germany, Italy, Netherlands, Portugal, Romania, Spain, and the UK. You can work from any office or remotely based in any of these countries.

FLEXIBLE SCHEDULE: Flexibility for us isn’t just about where we work—it also means being able to shape how and when we get things done. Together with their leaders, employees define schedules that align with their time zones, team needs, and personal routines.

PAID TIME OFF: We know how important it is to take time away from work to recharge. Employees receive a minimum of 25 days paid holiday per year with an additional day for each year of tenure (up to 5) in addition to annual holidays (including an extra holiday on your birthday!). 

PARENTAL LEAVE: Welcoming a new child is one of the most special moments in your life. Take the time to be present and enjoy your growing family. We offer 100% paid parental leave to all new parents. Parents giving birth are eligible for an extended leave and a ramp-back period to return part-time while they get settled. 

CAREER GROWTH: Access world-class platforms, participate in interactive sessions, build your personalized development roadmap, and explore internal opportunities. We focus on continuous learning and feedback to support your journey toward personal and professional success. 

CULTURE: You’ll join a team of passionate people who come together to break boundaries, support each other, and create a meaningful impact in workplace wellness. We win together, building trust through open communication and a culture where every perspective matters. Learn more about our shared culture and values here. 

Want to see what it’s really like to work here? Follow us on Instagram @lifeatwellhub and watch our team video on YouTube ! 

Diversity, Equity, and Belonging at Wellhub 

We aim to create a collaborative, supportive, and inclusive space where everyone knows they belong. 

Wellhub is committed to creating a diverse work environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, non-disqualifying physical or mental disability, national origin, veteran status, or any other basis covered by appropriate law.

Our commitment to inclusion also extends to how we recognize and reward our people. We’re proud to be Syndio Fair Pay Certified, reflecting our ongoing dedication to equitable and fair pay practices across our global team. Read more about it here. 

Questions on how we treat your personal data? See our Job Applicant Privacy Notice.

title: Senior Manager, Global Procurement
description:
ABOUT QUINCE 

Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.

What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.

OUR CULTURE 

Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.

- We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA. Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.

- Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths. 

- Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory. 

If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.

We are looking for multiple exceptional Senior Manager, Global Procurement for different categories including

- Senior Manager, Global Procurement - Apparel 

- Senior Manager, Global Procurement - Women's Knits & Tops 

- Senior Manager, Global Procurement - Men's and Women's Sweaters 

- Senior Manager, Global Procurement - Men's and Women's Activewear 

- Senior Manager, Global Procurement - Loungewear, Swimwear, KBM 

- Senior Manager, Global Procurement - Footwear 

You will own and drive cost structures and savings. This role is critical to our goal of delivering the highest quality products, at radically low prices, done right. Reporting to the Head of Procurement, the ideal candidate will leverage their deep expertise in commodity costing, clean sheet, manufacturing excellence & efficiency (consumption,C&M excellence), harvest timing, raw material availability to craft a competitive costing environment where major T1 and T2 suppliers are being challenged to provide transparent and competitive pricing to achieve a win win supply chain for both Quince and our partners.

Success in this role means achieving product cost at or near should-costing, securing supply continuity, and contributing to product excellence by aligning material procurement processes with the company’s innovation and sustainability goals. This role offers the opportunity to make a significant impact on our business, contribute to company growth, and shape the future of our global sourcing strategy.

Responsibilities 

- Procurement Category Strategy: Define and execute the commercial roadmap and vendor distribution strategy for assigned categories to improve margins as Quince scales. Establish short- and long-term procurement targets aligned to business growth.

- Consistently deliver exceptional product cost without sacrificing product quality or ESG considerations, including Procurement.

- Partner with the technology team to embed procurement capabilities and playbook into the Vendor Portal and Product Catalog tools.

- Identify and deliver 700 bps product cost reductions over the next 12 months.

- RFP Ownership & Execution: Structure and run competitive, end-to-end bidding processes to secure optimal cost and commercial terms with manufacturing partners. Own the full lifecycle from vendor identification through award.

- Deliver immediate, best-in-class product cost savings through rigorous negotiation, while simultaneously institutionalizing repeatable negotiation frameworks to build long-term category maturity and sustainable competitive advantage.

- Build AI agent to help us run RFP systematically in 2026 with the capability to build scenario analyses.

- Clean Sheet & Buy Plan Approvals: Create and utilize component-level “clean sheets” to drive pricing transparency; review, approve, and solution to optimum cost for all buy events within your categories.

- Current mature / scale categories: Ensure scale / cleansheet costing with Finished Goods Manufacturers / Negotiate upstream of Finished Goods to secure best pricing and availability of (inputs (e.g. fabrics, yarns, fibers, commodities, trims) new categories & new products

- Lead Buy Plan margin review to govern company margin targetPartner with material sourcing team to ensure transparent, competitive pricing from all key material suppliers (we own material, we own costing)

- Negotiate reasonable launch costing and set schedule (monthly, quarterly, at trigger points) to renegotiate for scale pricing as the business grows

- Support merchandising team by providing scale costing targets (i.e. what cost is achievable at scale)

- Upstream Sourcing: Partner directly with the Material Manager, Sourcing Teams and Tier 1 and Tier 2 vendors to align on, and implement, material benefits into finished goods costing.

- Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate upstream material availability into product design and development cycles, ensuring early-stage cost optimization and seamless material-to-finished-good transitions.

- Value Creation: Identify and execute on opportunities to reshape the supply chain and extract new financial value beyond traditional sourcing boundaries, including verticalization and volume consolidation plays. 

- e.g. How do we become a market maker for Cashmere, Silk, etc? Could we sell cashmere and silk to other retailers? How can we partner with other mills or manufacturers to build a verticalized supply chain for critical materials, like linen, from French/Belgian farms and scutchers to linen mills? How do we buy/sell commodities to manage price fluctuations (e.g. gold pricing, Cashmere pricing)?

Qualifications 

- 8+ years of experience in global procurement, sourcing, or supply chain management in retail apparel environment

- Proven track record running competitive RFP processes with international manufacturing partners

- Hands-on experience building and leveraging clean sheets for cost negotiation

- Strong analytical skills and comfort with data-driven decision making

- Experience working cross-functionally with merchandising, materials, and production teams

- Technical aptitude for leveraging AI-powered platforms (e.g., LLMs) to conduct scenario analysis and automate complex procurement tasks

- Excellent negotiation skills and commercial acumen

- Experience in apparel, soft goods, or home goods strongly preferred

- Bachelor’s degree required; MBA or advanced degree a plus

WHY QUINCE? 

Joining Quince means being part of a mission-driven team reshaping retail. You will work alongside talented colleagues, tackle meaningful challenges, and contribute to building a more sustainable, accessible future for customers and partners alike.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY & HIRING INTEGRITY 

Quince provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applications for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran or military status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. 

Quince is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities. If you need a reasonable accommodation to complete your application or to perform the essential functions of a role at Quince, please let us know by completing this accommodation form . We review all requests individually and will work with you to determine appropriate accommodations on a case-by-case basis.

Employment is contingent upon successful completion of a background check. Quince will conduct background checks in compliance with applicable federal, state, and local laws.

Security Advisory: Beware of Frauds 

At Quince, we're dedicated to recruiting top talent who share our drive for innovation. To safeguard candidates, Quince emphasizes legitimate recruitment practices. Initial communication is primarily via official Quince email addresses and LinkedIn; beware of deviations. Personal data and sensitive information will not be solicited during the application phase. Interviews are conducted via phone, in person, or through the approved platforms Google Meets or Zoom—never via messaging apps or other calling services. Offers are merit-based, communicated verbally, and followed up in writing. If personal information is requested to initiate the hiring process, rest assured it will be through secure and protected means.

title: Senior Partner Marketing Manager - Cloud & Channel
description:
Datadog’s Partner Marketing Team is looking for a Senior Partner Marketing Manager to drive strategic marketing initiatives with our Cloud Service Providers and Channel Partners in EMEA. In this role, you will own and execute marketing programs designed to increase partner engagement, generate leads, and expand awareness of Datadog’s solutions within the cloud provider and channel ecosystem. This position offers a high-impact opportunity to collaborate with cross-functional teams and senior leadership while shaping Datadog’s presence with our ecosystem of partners.

At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds, and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them. 

What You’ll Do: 

- Develop and execute regional partner marketing programs, including webinars, demand generation campaigns, enablement sessions, industry events, and social media initiatives to drive engagement.

- Set cross-team strategy and execute plans, working cross-functionally across product, demand gen, and partnerships teams — often in ambiguous, fast-changing environments.

- Drive coordinated field alignment, co-sell motions, and partner-led pipeline with AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure

- Understand and work within regions and stakeholders across the South EMEA region to build the partner ecosystem 

- Track and analyze the effectiveness of partner marketing initiatives, reporting on key performance metrics through internal and external quarterly OKRs to ensure continuous optimization.

- Translate partnership data into clear ROI narratives for leadership and client/partner audiences.This includes presenting partnership marketing strategies and results to stakeholders while demonstrating clear ROI and strategic value

- Build and own our EMEA presence at global conferences like AWS Reinvent, DASH and Google Cloud Next 

Who You Are: 

- 6-8 years of experience working in marketing; partner marketing and/or high-tech B2B marketing preferred

- Fluent in English (Datadog’s business language). Italian, Spanish or Arabic are nice to have.

- Strong stakeholder management and executive-level communication skills - the ability to build trust and influence across internal teams and partner organizations of varying sizes and seniority.

- You have a track record of turning co-marketing programs into pipeline - past campaigns generated measurable marketing-sourced revenue

- You are a strategic and analytical thinker paired with hands-on execution — you are equally comfortable setting vision and rolling up sleeves to run campaigns.

- Strong project management skills

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills with a proven ability to influence others

- You have experience with Salesforce or similar CRM tools

- Comfortable utilising AI in daily work

- This role requires 3 days a week in office

- Ability to travel 20% of the time

Datadog values people from all walks of life. We understand not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That's okay. If you’re passionate about technology and want to grow your skills, we encourage you to apply. 

Benefits and Growth: 

- New hire stock equity (RSU) and employee stock purchase plan (ESPP)

- Continuous professional development, product training, and career pathing 

- Intra-departmental mentor and buddy program for in-house networking 

- An inclusive company culture, opportunity to join our Community Guilds

- Generous and competitive benefits package

- Continuous career development and pathing opportunities 

Benefits and Growth listed above may vary based on the country of your employment and the nature of your employment with Datadog. 

About Datadog: 

Datadog is the leading observability and security platform for the AI era, providing businesses with unified visibility across the technology stack to manage complexity at scale. It brings applications, infrastructure, data, models, and security into one place, using AI to detect and resolve issues before they impact customers. Trusted globally by Fortune 500 companies and high-growth AI leaders, Datadog enables businesses to move faster with clarity and confidence. title: Content Editor
Sales Engineer
description:
At Gigaton, we’re on a mission to cut gigatonnes of carbon emissions from the world’s biggest emitting industries (like cement, steel and glass), by building autonomous AI control and optimisation systems that learn and leverage the physics of manufacturing. Our products run heavy industrial plants more efficiently, more stably, and with lower emissions in real time - laying the foundation for the next industrial revolution.

We are a team of scientists, engineers, builders, and operators who love hard problems, have high standards, and want to make change happen in the physical world. We care about deep tech, but we care even more about whether it delivers cost and carbon impact in a live plant, with real people, under real constraints.

With Gigaton, you’ll solve really tough problems in places few people ever get close to, and build something that actually helps the planet. Are you up for the challenge?

About the role

We are looking for a sales engineer to join our sales team and drive the frontline of industrial decarbonisation.

This role bridges the technical and commercial worlds. You'll need interpersonal and technical skills to build relationships with process engineers in cement plants and understand their challenges. Analytical skills will be essential to delve deep into complex plant data and work out how Gigaton's AI products can solve their most critical issues.

Building on that, you'll need strategic thinking and commercial awareness to turn your findings into concise, compelling proposals for decision-makers at our customers, from the C-suite down.

Ultimately, you'll build clarity from uncertainty, making sure we agree a shared roadmap with our customers that puts our solutions on track for significant real-world benefits before a contract is signed.

Over time, you’ll help us evolve our sales approach and shape the product by feeding insights and needs from the plant back to the product team, building the foundation for scaling across industries.

Your main responsibilities

- Be the technical expert on sales calls and visits with cement plants.

- Build trust with process engineers and plant teams by understanding their specific plant issues and linking them to how we can help.

- Analyse plant data to identify and evaluate opportunities, then use this analysis to create compelling sales proposals.

- Lead technical discovery and identify early when a plant does not meet our ICP (ideal customer profile) criteria.

- Make sure relationships and plant understanding are handed over successfully to the deployment team.

- Act as a feedback loop into Gigaton’s product and machine learning teams, providing field insights that help shape our product roadmap.

- Develop and iterate the pre-sales technical process, making it more impactful and more automated each time.

- Travel to plants and conferences , around one week per month, to understand customer environments and explain the product.

What a great fit looks like

- Exposure to physical sciences, controls, or heavy industry , such as cement, steel, energy, manufacturing, or similar.

- Strong analytical skills and an outcome-oriented mindset. You can dig into industrial data, identify root causes, generate potential solutions, and explain their value in dollars and tonnes of CO2.

- Excellent communication skills . You can build credibility and trust in complex industrial environments with both engineers and board-level stakeholders.

- Comfortable being the technical voice in the conversation , presenting to senior plant leaders and operators, handling objections, and being challenged on your findings by people who have run kilns for 30 years.

- Naturally curious and keen to learn about the industry, the technology, and each individual plant. You want to understand the root cause behind every question and objection so you can solve the right problem.

- Confident in ambiguity and able to field very specific technical questions without getting flustered. You know when you can give your understanding, when you need to go and find the answer, and how to maintain customer confidence in both situations.

- Willingness to travel regularly .

You’ll excel if

- You build trust easily . You can connect with plant engineers, listen deeply, and align solutions to their priorities.

- You’d rather diagnose than pitch . Your first instinct in a plant is to ask a better question, not to open the deck.

- You thrive in dynamic environments . Fast-paced, ambiguous settings excite you, and you’re motivated by high-impact, mission-driven work.

- You have experience working in heavy industry , particularly cement, steel, energy, heavy manufacturing, or similar.

Success in This Role Means

- Plants say yes because the technical case is clear. You build customer confidence that Gigaton can deliver high ROI, helping us hit our revenue goals without losing deals because customers don’t understand or believe in our product and capabilities.

- Deployments are set up to succeed . We haven’t overpromised to sign a contract, and our pre-contract analysis holds up once the system is live.

- Process engineers trust and rely on you as a partner in solving problems.

- Deals don’t stall waiting on a technical answer . Objections get handled quickly, and customers get the answers they need in good time.

💡 You are not expected to check every box, and we’d love to hear from you even if your experience isn’t an exact match. 

We’re building a team that reflects the world we want to change. Our people come from all walks of life, with different countries, cultures, and experiences, and we think that’s one of our biggest strengths.

We’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone feels safe, respected, and celebrated. No matter your background, if you’re excited by what we do, we want to hear from you.

The interview process

- Talent Partner Screen Call: Meet our talent partner and learn more about Gigaton and the role.

- Hiring Manager Screen: Meet our VP of Sales and discuss if this role is a good fit for you.

- Technical Onsite (completed on the same day):

- Technical interview 

- Data analysis & presentation 

- Operating Principles Interview: Understand how we work and whether Gigaton and you are a good fit for each other.

- Meet with the CEO: Every new potential hire meets Josh.

We believe hiring is a two-way process. Just as we’ll reference-check candidates before making a final offer, we encourage you to reference-check us by chatting to team members you haven’t yet met. Ask anything. We’ll answer with Concrete Honesty.

Once interviews are done, we’ll move quickly to a decision, and we’re always happy to give feedback at any stage.

In return for your hard work, we’ll give you 

📈 Equity in the company: When we win, you win. You’ll get share options, so you’re part of our journey from the inside.

🕰️ Flexible working We trust you to know how and when you work best and to work that out with your team.

🌴 30 days of holiday (plus bank holidays). Rest is productive. Take the time you need to recharge

🪙 A generous pension scheme. We’re planning for the future in more ways than one.

Our Operating Principles 

↗️ Go Gig or Go Home : High Bar, All In. What we do matters to humanity, to our customers and to each other. We hold ourselves to an extraordinarily high bar and bring the urgency this mission requires.

🏭 Concrete Honesty : Be honest. As concrete forms the foundation of our world, genuine honesty and transparency are the bedrock of our culture.

🦾 Autonomous Ownership : High agency, high ownership. We build systems that take control and make things better. We do the same: see it, own it, drive it.

😄 Cement it with Kindness & Fun : Have fun, be kind. We're here to extend Earth's life, but ours is still limited. We want to enjoy the ride. To see these in full, go to Gigaton’s Operating Principles Notion page.

title: Commercial Customer Success Manager
description:
A little about us

incident.io is the AI software reliability platform trusted by engineering teams at Netflix, Etsy, and 2,000+ companies who can't afford downtime.

The stakes are real, the talent is insane, and somehow it's a genuinely lovely place to work. We all pull our weight, go the extra mile, and put in the bit of magic most companies don't have time for, all while having fun and never taking ourselves too seriously.

We've raised $96 million from Index Ventures, Insight Partners, and Point Nine, and we're growing fast. There's never been a better time to join.

The role in one line 

Customers trust us when things go wrong. We're the software reliability platform built to investigate, respond to and prevent incidents. As a Commercial CSM, you're the partner to our mid-market engineering teams - getting them onboarded, embedded and expanding their usage, and maturing their incident management and reliability as they grow.

What that looks like day to day 

Our Customer Success organisation is at the heart of incident.io . We're the team closest to our customers' hardest problems, and we're trusted to solve them. We believe in a customer-led product approach, working hand in hand with Product to uncover and address what each customer really needs. Our goal goes beyond satisfaction: we want to delight customers at every stage of their journey, and build long-term relationships grounded in trust, shared success and mutual growth.

You'll look after 70–80 Commercial customers: growth-oriented tech companies, mostly under 1,000 people, between $30k and $150k ARR each. Industry leaders like Vanta, Monday.com and Loom sit in this segment. Some are steady, some are scaling fast, and much of the job is knowing which is which, and what each one needs from you.

Most of your time goes to mid-market customers on our top-tier plan, where you're their dedicated CSM leading onboarding and adoption. You'll blend 1:1 time with scalable programmes to get teams to value quickly: best-practice sessions, end-user training, partnership and roadmap reviews. You'll also cover a subset of smaller customers in a low-touch capacity, leaning on usage data to spot risk and opportunity early.

Day to day, this is a high ownership role. You'll help customers navigate the product, unpick problems when they hit them, and keep everyone pointed at the outcomes their team actually cares about. You are responsible for proactively identifying expansion and upsell opportunities, and partnering with Sales and Expansion Account Managers to grow revenue within your accounts. Internally, you're the voice of the Commercial customer with Product, Engineering, Sales, Marketing and Support.

There's still a lot to build and a ton of opportunity for you to shape this segment. The Commercial motion works, but scaling and automating the customer journey is live work we're ramping up now - refining playbooks, automating the repeatable stuff, building the tooling and content that makes a portfolio this size easier to serve. We're AI-forward in how we approach it, so you'd be shaping this rather than inheriting it.

Who you are 

- You've carried a book of 40 to 100+ accounts and worked out how to be present across all of them without going quiet on half.

- You've sold to, or supported, technical people, whether that's engineering teams, on-call rotations or developer tools. You can hold your own in a technical conversation without needing to escalate every one of them.

- You've got commercial instincts. You spot the account that's about to double, you know what a growth signal looks like, and you know how to steer a renewal to a good outcome.

- You know what scaled CS looks like when it's done well. Playbooks, one-to-many programs, AI-assisted workflows. You don't need to have built them from scratch, but you've worked around them enough to have opinions on what you'd do differently.

- Half-built process doesn't rattle you. You'd rather fix the documentation than complain about it.

- You actually like being in a room with customers, and you'll get on a plane for the right one.

Supporting you 

We work hard and we think life outside work matters just as much. Our benefits pack is built to support both.

- Private medical insurance. Seriously good cover — we want you and the people you love to be looked after.

- Competitive annual leave. Showing up at your best requires switching off, and we make sure you have time to do that.

- First Friday of every month off. Yes, seriously.

- Enhanced pension. We put real money in, because future-you deserves better than an afterthought.

- Meaningful equity. We're rapidly scaling, and everyone who helps shape the outcome should share in it.

- Unlimited AI spend. For everyone, not just engineers. We're all-in on AI across the company, and we expect you to be too.

- Generous parental leave. The early days with a new baby matter more than anything we're doing here, and we want you to be present for them.

- Two budgets that have your back. £1000 to invest in your setup, £500 a year to invest in yourself.

Compensation: £75K – £100K • Offers Commission

- London • £75K – £100K • Offers Commission

title: Senior ML Engineer | Kimchi (LLM Inference Optimization)
description:
Why Cast AI?

Cast AI is an automation platform that operates cloud-native and AI infrastructure at scale. By embedding autonomous decision-making directly into Kubernetes and cloud environments, Cast AI continuously optimizes performance, reliability, and efficiency in production.
The old way doesn't work. As Kubernetes and AI environments grow, manual decisions don’t. Cast AI replaces tickets, alerts, and manual tuning with continuous automation that adapts infrastructure as conditions change. Efficiency and cost savings follow naturally from that automation.
Over 2,100 companies already rely on Cast AI, including Akamai, BMW, Cisco, FICO, HuggingFace, NielsenIQ, Swisscom, and TGS.

Global team, diverse perspectives 

We're headquartered in Miami, but our impact is international. We take a global and intentional approach to diversity. Today, Cast AI operates across 34 countries spanning Europe, North America, Latin America, and APAC, bringing a wide range of perspectives into how we build and lead.

Unicorn momentum 

In January 2026, we achieved unicorn status with a strategic investment from Pacific Alliance Ventures, the corporate venture arm of Shinsegae Group (a $50+ billion Korean conglomerate). Our valuation now exceeds $1 billion, and we're just getting started.

Join us as we build the future of autonomous infrastructure. 

About the role

Throughput. Latency. KV cache utilization.

Move those three numbers in the right direction, and two things happen: customers get faster, cheaper inference, and our margins improve. That's the entire thesis of this role. Every kernel you tune, every quantization scheme you ship, every scheduler tweak you land shows up directly in a customer's p99 and on our P&L.
This is a high-impact seat. It is also a high-autonomy seat as you'll be given the room to lead the technical direction of inference optimization at Kimchi, not execute someone else's roadmap.

The problem: running LLMs in production is a moving target. The "right" model and serving configuration for a workload depend on traffic shape, sequence-length distribution, batch dynamics, GPU SKU, memory bandwidth, quantization tolerance, and a dozen other variables that shift week to week. Most teams pick a model once, over-provision GPUs, and absorb the cost. Kimchi is the system that makes that decision automatically - continuously matching workloads to the most cost-efficient, best-performing LLM and serving configuration on a customer's infrastructure. We're building the optimization layer between the model and the hardware, and we need engineers who understand both sides deeply.

Stack 

Python; vLLM; SGLang; TensorRT-LLM; PyTorch; CUDA-adjacent tooling; Kubernetes; gRP; ClickHouse; PostgreSQL; GCP Pub/Sub; AWS / GCP / Azure; GitLab CI; ArgoCD; Prometheus; Grafana; Loki; Tempo.

Requirements:

- 5+ years building real ML systems, with a portfolio that shows depth in inference or training infrastructure (not just model training notebooks).

- Strong Python - production services, not scripts.

- Hands-on experience with at least one of vLLM, SGLang, or TensorRT-LLM, and a working mental model of why an inference engine performs the way it does on a given GPU.

- Fluency with quantization tradeoffs - you've measured quality regressions, not just compression ratios.

- Comfort with distributed systems: collective communication, sharding strategies, and the practical failure modes of multi-GPU and multi-node setups.

- A bias toward measurement. You instrument before you optimize, and you can tell the difference between a real win and a benchmark artifact.

- Self-direction. This role comes with a wide mandate; you should be excited by that, not unsettled by it.

Responsibilities:

- Push throughput. Continuous batching, speculative decoding, chunked prefill, kernel-level tuning across vLLM, SGLang, and TensorRT-LLM. Find the ceiling on each GPU SKU, then raise it.

- Cut latency. Attack TTFT and TPOT separately. Profile, identify the actual bottleneck (compute, memory bandwidth, scheduling, networking), and fix it - not the bottleneck you assumed.

- Get more out of the KV cache. Paged attention, prefix caching, eviction policies, cache reuse across requests, quantized KV. This is where a lot of the unrealized throughput lives, and it's an area you'll own.

- Quantize without regressing quality. INT8, INT4, FP8 across weights, activations, and KV. Empirical work: measure quality on real workloads, not just perplexity benchmarks.

- Shrink cold starts and memory footprint. Faster init, smarter weight loading, tighter memory accounting - the difference between a model that scales and one that doesn't.

- Scale across nodes. Distributed inference topologies, network-aware placement, checkpointing strategies that don't bottleneck on storage or interconnect.

- Set the technical direction. Decide what we benchmark, what we adopt, and what we build ourselves. Bring the team along with strong writeups and reproducible experiments.

What’s in it for you?

- Competitive salary (depending on the level of experience).

- Enjoy a flexible, remote-first global environment.

- Collaborate with a global team of cloud experts and innovators, passionate about pushing the boundaries of Kubernetes technology

- Equity options.

- Get quick feedback with a fast-paced workflow. Most feature projects are completed in 1 to 4 weeks.

- Spend 10% of your work time on personal projects or self-improvement. 

- Learning budget for professional and personal development - including access to international conferences and courses that elevate your skills.

- Annual hackathon to spark new ideas and strengthen team bonds.

- Team-building budget and company events to connect with your colleagues.

- Equipment budget to ensure you have everything you need.

- Extra days off to help maintain a healthy work-life balance.

Hiring process

- Technical interview (system design)

- Live coding

Hi, we're DuckDuckGo, the online protection company and remote-first team of 300+ on a mission to raise the standard of trust online. Founded in 2008 and profitable since 2014, annual revenue now exceeds $100m USD and millions use our browser on Mac , Windows , iOS , and Android , our search engine , and the latest — Privacy Pro . Our culture of trust, inclusivity, and empowered project management underpins everything we do, where each team member takes full ownership of their projects, from scoping and execution to postmortem. If you're seeking end-to-end ownership of your work — you've come to the right place!

Your Team and Role 

Working on the Web Dependability Engineering team, you'll make sure websites just work in DuckDuckGo's browsers across Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android, helping ensure our users have the best-possible experience browsing with DuckDuckGo. Recent projects include:

- Reverse-engineering how sites detect our privacy protections and building countermeasures that keep pages working

- Shimming browser APIs so sites work seamlessly across different browser engines and system webviews

- Building LLM agent pipelines that automatically reproduce and triage reported site breakage

As a Senior Web Compatibility Engineer , you'll be our resident expert on why websites break and how to fix them: owning the webcompat side of our triage process, debugging gnarly issues in code you don't control, distinguishing site bugs from browser bugs from privacy protection-induced breakage, leading the charge when a top site breaks and becomes an incident, shipping durable fixes across every platform, and work on related projects that prevent user churn and keep users coming back to DuckDuckGo.

About You 

- 7+ years of experience building and debugging complex web applications with vanilla JavaScript.

- Detailed knowledge of web standards, web components, and browser APIs. Any additional experience with our stack is a bonus: Swift/Kotlin/C#/C++/Python.

- Advanced ability to reverse-engineer obfuscated third-party code and reduce issues to minimal test cases.

- Passion for hunting elusive bugs and tracing them to their root cause.

- Interest in automating repetitive work and building agentic tooling that multiplies the team's impact.

- Experience triaging issues, leading incident response, and communicating clearly with technical and non-technical stakeholders.

- Experience shipping code beyond the web, like native or desktop clients.

- Ability to lead complex, ambiguous projects with little to no oversight.

Compensation 

$178,500 USD annually and stock options. Compensation is identical within professional levels , regardless of geographic location or team. Compensation for each professional level is transparent across the organization. 

Eligibility for company-sponsored health benefits is limited to team members based in the United States. This program does not extend to team members located in other countries, such as Canada or the UK.

The Order Taking squad owns core ordering experiences within SumUp’s Point of Sale app, including the shopping bag, checkout, the catalog experience within ordering, open orders, table management and printer integrations. As a Senior iOS Engineer, you’ll build new hospitality workflows and evolve established ordering experiences across iOS and Android. You’ll work with SwiftUI on the platform-specific UI and contribute to shared Kotlin Multiplatform business logic. The role involves complex mobile engineering across multi-device synchronisation, shared order state and a large, established application.

You’ll join a small, experienced and fast-moving squad that works collaboratively through technical refinement, code reviews and pair programming. The team values engineers who communicate directly, challenge assumptions and proactively shape solutions rather than simply execute predefined tasks.

- Design and build new ordering experiences in SwiftUI, while evolving established capabilities such as table management, kitchen workflows and printer integrations

- Contribute to shared Kotlin Multiplatform business logic and help shape the architecture of the ordering domain

- Improve the reliability and usability of ordering features used daily by hospitality merchants across phones, tablets and POS devices

- Take part in code reviews, pair programming and collaborative testing to maintain a high quality bar

- Help refine and scope upcoming work, bringing technical judgement to product and architectural trade-offs

- Contribute to Mobile Chapter and KMP platform initiatives across the wider POS tribe

You'll be great for this role if... 

- 5+ years of experience building production iOS applications in Swift, with strong SwiftUI knowledge

- Experience working in a large, established codebase and making pragmatic improvements without requiring a full rewrite

- Openness to learning and contributing to Kotlin and Kotlin Multiplatform; previous hands-on KMP experience is welcome but not required

- Ability to work independently, challenge assumptions, propose solutions proactively and communicate clearly and directly

- Experience collaborating closely with Android engineers or other cross-platform partners to align product behaviour

- Sound technical judgement and the ability to balance product delivery, code quality and long-term maintainability

Why you should join SumUp 

🌎 Opportunity to work with a truly global, multicultural team from our Paris location. This involves an office-first setup

En tant que Business Development Representative chez Amenitiz, vous prenez en charge l'intégralité du cycle de vente, du premier contact de prospection jusqu'à la signature du contrat. Vous prospectez, réalisez des démonstrations, traitez les objections et concluez les ventes, tout en gérant votre pipeline et votre contribution au chiffre d'affaires de bout en bout.

Nos clients sont des hôteliers indépendants partout en Europe : des établissements familiaux, des hôtels-boutiques et de petites chaînes hôtelières insuffisamment servis par des solutions technologiques conçues pour les grands groupes. Avec plus de 15 000 clients et une note de satisfaction de 4,8/5, notre produit bénéficie d'une forte reconnaissance sur le marché.

Vous commercialiserez une solution qui a un impact concret et mesurable sur le quotidien de ses utilisateurs, tout en étant pleinement responsable de l'ensemble du processus qui leur permet d'y accéder.

(Ce rôle est basé à Lyon, en France)

- Gestion des objections et closing

- Traitez avec assurance les hésitations, les comparaisons avec la concurrence et les objections liées au timing. Créez un sentiment d'urgence lorsque cela est pertinent et sachez demander la signature.

- Collaboration

- Travaillez en étroite collaboration avec les responsables commerciaux et vos collègues afin d'améliorer en continu votre approche. Partagez les retours du marché, les objections récurrentes et les informations concurrentielles pour contribuer à la performance collective.

- Vous disposez de 2 à 4 ans d'expérience dans une fonction commerciale (SDR, Account Executive ou poste en cycle de vente complet).

- Vous êtes de langue maternelle française, italienne, espagnole ou portugaise, et possédez un excellent niveau d'anglais, à l'écrit comme à l'oral.

- Vous êtes à l'aise pour alterner entre des phases de prospection intensive et des phases de closing au cours d'une même semaine.

title: Senior Software Engineer - Paris
description:
About H: 

When we released Holo4 on 28 September, we published every trajectory behind its public benchmark scores at trajectories.hcompany.ai . For OSWorld that's 369 desktop tasks, each run 3 times, with the steps, tokens and time of every attempt. This role builds and runs the evaluation framework that produces runs like these.

H builds computer-use agents and the models behind them. Developers use them through a managed API , and our forward deployed engineers take them into enterprise workflows.

What this team owns

The evaluation framework: orchestration, runtimes and observability. Researchers and forward deployed engineers bring the benchmarks, across web apps, desktop applications and the command line. Your job is to make the framework that runs them reliable, fast and cheap, and to make adding a new one quick. Research uses the results to choose checkpoints and decide whether a model ships. Product and the forward deployed engineers use them to measure agents on customer workflows. It carries roughly 50 benchmarks now. That number should be between 100 and 200 soon, and the framework has to keep up.

What you'd be doing

- Integration support for researchers and forward deployed engineers bringing in a benchmark, with a shorter path each time.

- Setting the standard for how a benchmark enters the framework, and building the checks that enforce it.

- Scheduling and observability, so cluster capacity isn't left idle while evaluation jobs queue.

- Reproducible results across trials, so a release decision rests on numbers that hold.

- Whatever stack a benchmark calls for. One week that's cluster tuning; the next it's a browser extension or desktop environments.

- Time with customers, from single developers to large companies, to find out what they want measured, then automating it so the results flow back into our harnesses and models.

The first few months

By 3 months you'll have helped researchers or forward deployed engineers integrate 5 benchmarks, and started fixing what slows the framework down. By 6 months one part of it is yours, for example scaling the runs, observability, or a group of related benchmarks, and a release will have gone out on your numbers. By 12 months you'll know the design and trade-offs of the whole evaluation system, and be the person the rest of H asks about evaluations.

Who you'd work with

Ceiran Chapman, our VP Engineering, is hiring for this role. You'd join the evaluation team. The people relying on your work day to day are H's researchers and forward deployed engineers.

What we think it takes

Likely a good fit if you 

- Have spent 5+ years in backend development, with production Python at the core, and use coding agents to go faster without letting quality drop.

- Have built test, QA or evaluation tooling that other teams depended on, and care whether a number is right.

- Have operated distributed systems on Kubernetes in a public cloud. AWS experience helps most.

- Have built and shipped systems end to end, including APIs (REST or GraphQL) and integrations with outside services.

- Know relational and non-relational databases, and message queues such as SQS, RabbitMQ or Kafka.

- Instrument what you build, with metrics, tracing and monitoring from the start.

Stronger still if you have 

- Measured LLM quality before, or built agents yourself.

- Packaged and run workloads in Docker and on virtual machines.

- Used Temporal, Dask, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Grafana or Datadog.

- Automated web or desktop software with Playwright, Selenium or a browser extension you wrote.

- Set standards other engineers follow, through code review, design review or mentoring.

You do not need a background in machine learning. We'll work that out with you. If you match most of this but not all of it, apply anyway.

How we hire

A 30 minute call with our Talent team, a 60 minute technical challenge, a 60 minute system design interview, and a 30 minute final conversation with Ceiran. About 3.5 hours in total.

Practicalities

Paris posting: Hybrid in Paris. That means 3 office days a week and a London trip about once every 4 to 6 weeks. There is a London posting for the same role. We offer a competitive package.

title: Automation Lead
description:
About us, and our mission 

At Orakl Oncology, we are accelerating the development of oncology treatments. Today, fewer than 5% of new cancer drugs succeed in clinical trials. Clearly, new methods are needed. We combine cutting-edge biology and AI to build the next generation of insight platforms with a large cohort of patient-derived tumor avatars. These avatars fuel our predictive engine, helping to anticipate clinical outcomes, validate therapies and uncover new drug candidates. By generating multimodal, real-world data, we aim to make drug development smarter, faster and more personalized. We collaborate with leading hospitals, research institutes and pharmaceutical companies. Backed by leading investors, Orakl is a fast-growing, mission-driven startup at the intersection of biology, automation and AI.

Position overview 

Orakl runs a high-throughput 3D cell‑culture platform to culture patient-derived organoids (PDOs). These patient-derived specimens reveal critical information into the patient disease, but require heavy maintenance work. Automating these workflows will be critical to improve the reliability and traceability of experimental work. We are hiring our first automation lead to build the Automation function from scratch. This is a high ownership and high autonomy job. You will map our processes, decide what to automate and what to leave alone, specify and source the equipment, negotiate with vendors and integrators, commission the machines, run them with the lab team, and hire the people the function needs. As the ideal candidate, you have already put automated lines or special machines into service, and you know what typically breaks between commissioning and the first experimental runs. While previous experience in biology is a plus, it is not a strict requirement: you will be taught all you need to know. However, you do need a proven experience in working deeply embedded in interdisciplinary teams.

Key responsibilities 

- Map cell culture workflows end to end and identify key process automation and optimisation opportunities.

- Own the automation roadmap. Present and lead the implementation of the major decisions to Orakl’s leadership.

- In line with the automation strategy you will have identified, evaluate vendors and integrators. Write user requirement specifications, acceptance criteria and interface requirements for each project.

- Negotiate price, scope, delivery, acceptance, support and consumables terms autonomously within agreed thresholds.

- Lead design reviews and factory and site acceptance tests.

- Translate our proprietary cell culture protocols into automated machine execution with our team of cell biologists and scientists.

- Track machine availability, hands-on time per line, interventions, failures and recovery time. Use the data to decide the next step.

- Coordinate with Orakl’s management to anticipate future automation needs on the platform and adjust the roadmap accordingly.

- Hire and develop the automation technicians and engineers the roadmap needs.

- Set the standards for the automated platform: documentation, quality control, safety, qualification, change control, vendor management.

In this role you will collaborate closely with our cell culture, cell biology and data science teams. You will be at the heart of Orakl Oncology’s capabilities roadmap and help generate unprecedented amounts of biological data to power scientific discovery in cancer.

Key qualifications 

Must-have 

- Engineering degree (generalist, robotics, industrial, mechanical or process engineering) or equivalent, and at least eight years of experience.

- Exceptional process thinking skills: you map flows, time operations, find bottlenecks and question the processes.

- Experience in supplier negotiation and budget ownership on your own projects.

- Experience in PLC and robot programming concepts, scheduling software, instrument interfaces, basic scripting.

- You enjoy and are comfortable spending time on the floor with operators. You have experience in communicating and operating with engineers, technicians and workers at the heart of production processes.

- Autonomy: you tell your manager what you decided and why, not what you need decided.

- Fluency in English is required.

Nice-to-have 

- You have put automated lines, cells or special machines into service end to end: requirements, vendor selection, negotiation, integration, factory and site acceptance, ramp-up, budget. This doesn’t have to be in a lab environment : plant, food and fermentation, pharma or cosmetics are other examples of relevant experience.

- Automation in life-science or regulated environments: cell culture, biotech, food and fermentation, pharma, cleanroom or BSL-2 work.

- A working understanding of cell culture and what it demands: sterility, contamination risk, variability between samples, and steps governed by the biological pace.

- Liquid handling, plate-based workflows, incubators and imagers; laboratory scheduling software.

- Experience hiring and leading an automation team.

What we offer 

- You will be Orakl's first automation hire. You will have a unique degree of ownership and scope with a strong mandate to deliver.

- Short decision lines and fast execution.

- An interdisciplinary environment with a results-driven culture.

Recruitment process 

- Introductory call with Talent / People — 20 minutes

- Interview with the Lab Director, hiring manager — 45 minutes, including a 15-minute live mini-case on a small lab process

- Technical deep dive with the CTO and the Lab Director

- Case study on a real part of our lab: a take-home capped at four hours, then a half day on site with presentation, challenge round, lab walk.

- Cross-functional interviews with the technicians who run the culture, Platform Operations, the Senior Laboratory Engineers and the Data team — 60 minutes

- Reference calls: a former manager, a vendor or integrator you negotiated with, and an operator who ran a line you delivered

- Founder conversation — 45 minutes

Our Values: 

Working at Mirakl means accelerating your career alongside ambitious, passionate, and supportive colleagues. We're proud of the diversity of backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences that make our teams unique.

Our 5 values guide how we collaborate:

- 💡 Work Hard Together: Teamwork and collaboration are the foundation of our success

- 🏆 Get Things Done: We prioritize action and efficiency for impactful results

The Team You'll Join 

You'll join the Product team within Mirakl Platform, working on the Catalog Management pillar.
You'll work at the intersection of product, data, and AI: using AI to make our team faster, and helping design the AI agents our customers will use inside Mirakl.

This is a 6-month internship starting in January/February 2027. You'll participate in team rituals, gain autonomy quickly, and have the opportunity to present your work regularly to management, offering strong visibility within the organization.

Role & Mission 

You will be the operational backbone of Alta Ares' field demonstration team — ensuring that every client and partner demonstration runs flawlessly, from equipment preparation through to mission debrief.

On the ground, you are the go-to support for pilots, operators, and engineers: handling logistics, setting up and dismantling demo sites, keeping the equipment fleet in condition, and solving problems on the fly. Your versatility and resourcefulness set you apart — you move seamlessly from a hardware check to a client interaction, from a flight case to a transport declaration, without losing pace or precision.

Key Responsibilities

Demonstration Preparation 

- Prepare and verify all equipment before each mission: drones, ground control stations, batteries, and tooling

- Pack into flight cases and conduct pre-departure checks

- Keep inventories accurate and up to date

Checklists & Continuous Improvement 

- Own the operational and equipment checklists — execute them on the day

- Update checklists after each mission based on field feedback

- Formalise and improve processes continuously

Logistics & Transport 

- Organise outbound shipments and equipment returns

- Prepare all transport documentation and coordinate with carriers and the supply chain

- Ensure material arrives on time and in compliance with applicable regulations, including for sensitive or dual-use equipment

Field Deployment 

- Install and strike the demonstration site

- Support pilots during flight operations

- Serve as the on-site point of contact for ground teams, host nation staff, and client representatives

Equipment Maintenance 

- Monitor the condition of the demonstration fleet and report anomalies

- Carry out first-level maintenance interventions

- Keep the hardware mission-ready at all times

Administrative Support 

- Prepare authorisation requests and write mission reports

- Manage expense claims and travel bookings

- Keep tracking tools up to date: backlog, planning, and mission logs
